<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Adepta Sororitas (11 out of 16 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Acts of Faith</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is ADEPTA SORORITAS , each unit from your army with this ability can perform one Act of Faith per phase. This is done using Miracle dice. GAINING MIRACLE DICE If your Army Faction is ADEPTA SORORITAS , you gain 1 Miracle dice: - At the start of each battle round. - Each time an ADEPTA SORORITAS unit from your army is destroyed. Each time you gain a Miracle dice, roll one D6. The number you roll is the value of that Miracle dice. This value cannot be changed or re-rolled , unless a rule specifically states otherwise. Keep your Miracle dice to one side - this is your Miracle dice pool. PERFORMING AN ACT OF FAITH Before making a dice roll for a model or unit from your army with the Acts of Faith ability, if you have one or more dice in your Miracle dice pool, that unit can perform an Act of Faith. If it does, select one of the dice from your Miracle dice pool to substitute that dice roll (if a roll involves more than one dice, e.g. a Charge roll or Battle-shock test , only a single dice can be substituted). The dice that is being substituted is not rolled; instead, the value of the selected Miracle dice is used as if it had been rolled ( this counts as an unmodified dice roll of that value for all rules purposes). Each Miracle dice can only be selected for substitution once. Once all Miracle dice substitutions have been made, remove the chosen Miracle dice from your Miracle dice pool, and roll all remaining, unsubstituted dice that are a part of the dice roll. You can use Miracle dice when a unit performs an Act of Faith for any of the following types of dice roll: - Advance roll - Battle-shock test - Charge roll - Damage roll - Hit roll - Saving throw - Wound roll Example: Instead of rolling 2D6 to take a unit&#x27;s Battle-shock test, you could use one dice from your Miracle dice pool. If the value of that dice was 4, the unit&#x27;s Battle-shock test would be determined by rolling one D6 and adding 4 to it (i.e. it would be D6+4).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Miracle dice pool with per-phase Act usage and substitution tracking.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

Add 3&quot; to the Move characteristic of PENITENT models from your army. Absolution in Battle The penitents smite the Emperor&#x27;s foes with unmatched zeal. Each time a unit from your army is selected to fight, if that unit made a Charge move this turn, until the end of the phase, add 1 to the Attacks and Strength characteristics of melee weapons equipped by PENITENT models in that unit. Death Before Disgrace Even the most grievous wound cannot stop a penitent warrior in their quest to earn redemption in the eyes of the Emperor. Each time a PENITENT model from your army is destroyed by a melee attack, if that model has not fought this phase, roll one D6. On a 2+, do not remove it from play; the destroyed model can fight after the attacking unit has finished making its attacks, and is then removed from play.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No effect logic wired.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Acts of Faith</td><td><details><summary>37 units</summary>Aestred Thurga And Agathae Dolan<br/>Arco-flagellants<br/>Battle Sanctum<br/>Battle Sisters Squad<br/>Canoness<br/>Canoness with Jump Pack<br/>Castigator<br/>Celestian Insidiants<br/>Celestian Sacresant Aveline<br/>Celestian Sacresants<br/>Crusaders<br/>Daemonifuge<br/>Death Cult Assassins<br/>Dialogus<br/>Dogmata<br/>Dominion Squad<br/>Exorcist<br/>Hospitaller<br/>Imagifier<br/>Immolator<br/>Junith Eruita<br/>Ministorum Priest<br/>Mortifiers<br/>Morvenn Vahl<br/>Palatine<br/>Paragon Warsuits<br/>Penitent Engines<br/>Repentia Squad<br/>Repressor<br/>Retributor Squad<br/>Saint Celestine<br/>Sanctifiers<br/>Seraphim Squad<br/>Sisters Novitiate Squad<br/>Sororitas Rhino<br/>Triumph Of Saint Katherine<br/>Zephyrim Squad</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is ADEPTA SORORITAS , each unit from your army with this ability can perform one Act of Faith per phase. This is done using Miracle dice. GAINING MIRACLE DICE If your Army Faction is ADEPTA SORORITAS , you gain 1 Miracle dice: - At the start of each battle round. - Each time an ADEPTA SORORITAS unit from your army is destroyed. Each time you gain a Miracle dice, roll one D6. The number you roll is the value of that Miracle dice. This value cannot be changed or re-rolled , unless a rule specifically states otherwise. Keep your Miracle dice to one side - this is your Miracle dice pool. PERFORMING AN ACT OF FAITH Before making a dice roll for a model or unit from your army with the Acts of Faith ability, if you have one or more dice in your Miracle dice pool, that unit can perform an Act of Faith. If it does, select one of the dice from your Miracle dice pool to substitute that dice roll (if a roll involves more than one dice, e.g. a Charge roll or Battle-shock test , only a single dice can be substituted). The dice that is being substituted is not rolled; instead, the value of the selected Miracle dice is used as if it had been rolled ( this counts as an unmodified dice roll of that value for all rules purposes). Each Miracle dice can only be selected for substitution once. Once all Miracle dice substitutions have been made, remove the chosen Miracle dice from your Miracle dice pool, and roll all remaining, unsubstituted dice that are a part of the dice roll. You can use Miracle dice when a unit performs an Act of Faith for any of the following types of dice roll: - Advance roll - Battle-shock test - Charge roll - Damage roll - Hit roll - Saving throw - Wound roll Example: Instead of rolling 2D6 to take a unit&#x27;s Battle-shock test, you could use one dice from your Miracle dice pool. If the value of that dice was 4, the unit&#x27;s Battle-shock test would be determined by rolling one D6 and adding 4 to it (i.e. it would be D6+4).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Miracle dice pool with per-phase Act usage and substitution tracking.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>10 units</summary>Battle Sanctum<br/>Castigator<br/>Exorcist<br/>Immolator<br/>Junith Eruita<br/>Mortifiers<br/>Morvenn Vahl<br/>Penitent Engines<br/>Repressor<br/>Sororitas Rhino</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Canoness with Jump Pack<br/>Daemonifuge<br/>Saint Celestine<br/>Seraphim Squad<br/>Zephyrim Squad</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Arco-flagellants<br/>Celestian Sacresant Aveline<br/>Mortifiers<br/>Penitent Engines<br/>Repentia Squad</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Daemonifuge, Death Cult Assassins</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Repressor, Sororitas Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Death Cult Assassins, Sisters Novitiate Squad</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>13 units</summary>Aestred Thurga And Agathae Dolan<br/>Canoness<br/>Canoness with Jump Pack<br/>Dialogus<br/>Dogmata<br/>Hospitaller<br/>Imagifier<br/>Junith Eruita<br/>Ministorum Priest<br/>Morvenn Vahl<br/>Palatine<br/>Saint Celestine<br/>Triumph Of Saint Katherine</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Celestian Sacresant Aveline, Daemonifuge, Death Cult Assassins</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Dominion Squad, Sanctifiers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>11 units</summary>Anathema Psykana Rhino<br/>Ares Gunship<br/>Caladius Grav-tank<br/>Contemptor-achillus Dreadnought<br/>Contemptor-galatus Dreadnought<br/>Coronus Grav-carrier<br/>Orion Assault Dropship<br/>Pallas Grav-attack<br/>Telemon Heavy Dreadnought<br/>Venerable Contemptor Dreadnought<br/>Venerable Land Raider</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>12 units</summary>Allarus Custodians<br/>Aquilon Custodians<br/>Blade Champion<br/>Custodian Guard<br/>Custodian Guard With Adrasite And Pyrithite Spears<br/>Custodian Wardens<br/>Sagittarum Custodians<br/>Shield-captain<br/>Shield-captain In Allarus Terminator Armour<br/>Trajann Valoris<br/>Valerian<br/>Venatari Custodians</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Aleya, Trajann Valoris, Valerian</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Anathema Psykana Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Ares Gunship, Orion Assault Dropship</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Aleya<br/>Blade Champion<br/>Knight-centura<br/>Shield-captain<br/>Shield-captain In Allarus Terminator Armour<br/>Shield-captain On Dawneagle Jetbike<br/>Trajann Valoris<br/>Valerian</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Martial Ka&#x27;tah</td><td><details><summary>25 units</summary>Agamatus Custodians<br/>Allarus Custodians<br/>Aquilon Custodians<br/>Ares Gunship<br/>Blade Champion<br/>Caladius Grav-tank<br/>Contemptor-achillus Dreadnought<br/>Contemptor-galatus Dreadnought<br/>Coronus Grav-carrier<br/>Custodian Guard<br/>Custodian Guard With Adrasite And Pyrithite Spears<br/>Custodian Wardens<br/>Orion Assault Dropship<br/>Pallas Grav-attack<br/>Sagittarum Custodians<br/>Shield-captain<br/>Shield-captain In Allarus Terminator Armour<br/>Shield-captain On Dawneagle Jetbike<br/>Telemon Heavy Dreadnought<br/>Trajann Valoris<br/>Valerian<br/>Venatari Custodians<br/>Venerable Contemptor Dreadnought<br/>Venerable Land Raider<br/>Vertus Praetors</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Each time a unit from your army with this ability is selected to fight, select one of the Ka&#x27;tah Stances below. Until that unit has finished making its attacks, the selected Stance is active for it and it gains the relevant ability: Dacatarai Stance Those Custodians skilled in the Dacatarai Ka&#x27;tah are able to turn their enemies numerical advantage against them. Reserved for when the Custodians must battle seething hordes of foes, this stance sees them reap a terrible tally Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability. Rendax Stance Masters of Rendax are superlative monster and war machine hunters. They have studied every aspect of how to do battle with a foe far larger than themselves, how to evade its powerful attacks, exploit its blind spots and lay it low. Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [LETHAL HITS] ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight-phase Ka&#x27;tah selection with Lethal/Sustained hit hooks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Aleya, Knight-centura, Witchseekers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>11 units</summary>Archaeopter Fusilave<br/>Archaeopter Stratoraptor<br/>Archaeopter Transvector<br/>Ironstrider Ballistarii<br/>Kastelan Robots<br/>Onager Dunecrawler<br/>Skorpius Disintegrator<br/>Skorpius Dunerider<br/>Sydonian Dragoons With Radium Jezzails<br/>Sydonian Dragoons With Taser Lances<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td>Archaeopter Transvector, Pteraxii Skystalkers, Pteraxii Sterylizors, Terrax-pattern Termite</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Doctrina Imperatives</td><td><details><summary>36 units</summary>Archaeopter Fusilave<br/>Archaeopter Stratoraptor<br/>Archaeopter Transvector<br/>Belisarius Cawl<br/>Corpuscarii Electro-priests<br/>Cybernetica Datasmith<br/>Fulgurite Electro-priests<br/>Ironstrider Ballistarii<br/>Kastelan Robots<br/>Kataphron Breachers<br/>Kataphron Destroyers<br/>Onager Dunecrawler<br/>Pteraxii Skystalkers<br/>Pteraxii Sterylizors<br/>Secutarii Hoplites<br/>Secutarii Peltasts<br/>Serberys Raiders<br/>Serberys Sulphurhounds<br/>Servitor Battleclade<br/>Servitors<br/>Sicarian Infiltrators<br/>Sicarian Ruststalkers<br/>Skitarii Marshal<br/>Skitarii Rangers<br/>Skitarii Vanguard<br/>Skorpius Disintegrator<br/>Skorpius Dunerider<br/>Sydonian Dragoons With Radium Jezzails<br/>Sydonian Dragoons With Taser Lances<br/>Sydonian Skatros<br/>Tech-priest Dominus<br/>Tech-priest Enginseer<br/>Tech-priest Manipulus<br/>Technoarcheologist<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite<br/>X-101</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> At the start of the battle round, you can select one of the Doctrina Imperatives below. Until the end of the battle round, that Doctrina Imperative is active for your army, and all units from your army that have the Doctrina Imperatives ability gain the relevant abilities shown below. Protector Imperative - Ranged weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [HEAVY] ability. - Improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of ranged weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1. - Each time a melee attack targets this unit, if this unit has the BATTLELINE keyword and/or it is within 6&quot; of one or more friendly ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE units, subtract 1 from the Hit roll . Conqueror Imperative - Ranged weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [ASSAULT] ability. - Improve the Weapon Skill characteristic of melee weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1. - Each time a model in this unit makes an attack, if this unit has the BATTLELINE keyword and/or it is within 6&quot; of one or more friendly ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE units, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 1.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Round-based imperatives with WS/BS/AP/heavy/assault modifiers.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Corpuscarii Electro-priests, Fulgurite Electro-priests</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Skorpius Dunerider</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Archaeopter Fusilave, Archaeopter Stratoraptor, Archaeopter Transvector</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Sicarian Infiltrators</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Cybernetica Datasmith<br/>Skitarii Marshal<br/>Tech-priest Dominus<br/>Tech-priest Enginseer<br/>Tech-priest Manipulus<br/>Technoarcheologist</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Sydonian Skatros</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Serberys Raiders, Skitarii Rangers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Sicarian Infiltrators<br/>Sicarian Ruststalkers<br/>Sydonian Dragoons With Radium Jezzails<br/>Sydonian Dragoons With Taser Lances<br/>Sydonian Skatros</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Voice of Command</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is ASTRA MILITARUM , OFFICER models with this ability can issue Orders. Each OFFICER &#x27;s datasheet will specify how many Orders it can issue in a battle round and which units are eligible to receive those Orders. Each time an Officer model issues an Order, select one of the Orders below, then select one eligible friendly unit within 6&quot; of that Officer model to issue it to. OFFICER models can issue Orders in your Command phase and at the end of a phase in which they disembarked from a TRANSPORT or were set up on the battlefield. Until the start of your next Command phase, the unit you selected is affected by that Order. Unless otherwise stated, a unit can only be affected by one Order at a time (any Order subsequently issued to that unit replaces the current one). Orders cannot be issued to Battle-shocked units, and if a unit being affected by an Order becomes Battle-shocked, that Order ceases to affect that unit. Only ASTRA MILITARUM models gain the benefit of an Order issued to their unit. Move! Move! Move! M +3&quot; Add 3&quot; to the Move characteristic of models in this unit. Fix Bayonets! WS +1 Improve the Weapon Skill characteristic of melee weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1. Take Aim! BS +1 Improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of ranged weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1. First Rank, Fire! Second Rank, Fire! A +1 Improve the Attacks characteristic of Rapid Fire weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1. Take Cover! SV +1 Improve the Save characteristic of models in this unit by 1 (this cannot improve a model&#x27;s Save to better than 3+). Duty and Honour! LD +1 OC +1 Improve the Leadership and Objective Control characteristics of models in this unit by 1.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Order issuing in Command phase with stat modifiers.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Elysian Drop Sentinel<br/>Elysian Sniper Squad<br/>Hades Breaching Drill<br/>Militarum Tempestus Command Squad<br/>Tempestus Aquilons<br/>Tempestus Scions</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Bullgryn Squad<br/>Lord Marshal Dreir<br/>Nork Deddog<br/>Ogryn Bodyguard<br/>Ogryn Squad<br/>Sergeant Harker</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Gaunt&#x27;s Ghosts</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Banehammer<br/>Chimera<br/>Doomhammer<br/>Storm Chimera<br/>Stormlord</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Aquila Lander<br/>Arvus Lighter<br/>Valkyrie<br/>Valkyrie Sky Talon<br/>Vendetta Gunship<br/>Vulture Gunship</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Gaunt&#x27;s Ghosts<br/>Provisionally Prepared<br/>Ratlings<br/>Rein And Raus<br/>Sly Marbo</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>18 units</summary>Cadian Castellan<br/>Cadian Command Squad<br/>Catachan Command Squad<br/>Commissar<br/>Death Rider Commissar<br/>Hell&#x27;s Last<br/>Krieg Command Squad<br/>Lord Marshal Dreir<br/>Lord Solar Leontus<br/>Militarum Tempestus Command Squad<br/>Ministorum Priest<br/>Primaris Psyker<br/>Provisionally Prepared<br/>Quartermaster Cadre Squad<br/>Sergeant Harker<br/>Tech-Priest Enginseer<br/>Ursula Creed<br/>Iron Hand&#x27; Straken</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Gaunt&#x27;s Ghosts, Rein And Raus, Sly Marbo</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td><details><summary>11 units</summary>Catachan Command Squad<br/>Catachan Heavy Weapons Squad<br/>Catachan Jungle Fighters<br/>Kasrkin<br/>Krieg Combat Engineers<br/>Mukaali Riders<br/>Salamander Scout Vehicle<br/>Scout Sentinels<br/>Sergeant Harker<br/>Tauros Assault Vehicle<br/>Iron Hand&#x27; Straken</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Gaunt&#x27;s Ghosts<br/>Provisionally Prepared<br/>Ratlings<br/>Rein And Raus<br/>Sly Marbo</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Voice of Command</td><td><details><summary>16 units</summary>Cadian Castellan<br/>Cadian Command Squad<br/>Catachan Command Squad<br/>Commissar<br/>Death Rider Commissar<br/>Gaunt&#x27;s Ghosts<br/>Hell&#x27;s Last<br/>Krieg Command Squad<br/>Leman Russ Commander<br/>Lord Marshal Dreir<br/>Lord Solar Leontus<br/>Militarum Tempestus Command Squad<br/>Rogal Dorn Commander<br/>Sergeant Harker<br/>Ursula Creed<br/>Iron Hand&#x27; Straken</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is ASTRA MILITARUM , OFFICER models with this ability can issue Orders. Each OFFICER &#x27;s datasheet will specify how many Orders it can issue in a battle round and which units are eligible to receive those Orders. Each time an Officer model issues an Order, select one of the Orders below, then select one eligible friendly unit within 6&quot; of that Officer model to issue it to. OFFICER models can issue Orders in your Command phase and at the end of a phase in which they disembarked from a TRANSPORT or were set up on the battlefield. Until the start of your next Command phase, the unit you selected is affected by that Order. Unless otherwise stated, a unit can only be affected by one Order at a time (any Order subsequently issued to that unit replaces the current one). Orders cannot be issued to Battle-shocked units, and if a unit being affected by an Order becomes Battle-shocked, that Order ceases to affect that unit. Only ASTRA MILITARUM models gain the benefit of an Order issued to their unit. Move! Move! Move! M +3&quot; Add 3&quot; to the Move characteristic of models in this unit. Fix Bayonets! ### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>14 units</summary>Grand Master In Nemesis Dreadknight<br/>Grey Knights Dreadnought<br/>Grey Knights Relic Razorback<br/>Grey Knights Thunderhawk Gunship<br/>Land Raider<br/>Land Raider Crusader<br/>Land Raider Redeemer<br/>Nemesis Dreadknight<br/>Razorback<br/>Rhino<br/>Stormhawk Interceptor<br/>Stormraven Gunship<br/>Stormtalon Gunship<br/>Venerable Dreadnought</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>19 units</summary>Brother-captain<br/>Brother-captain Stern<br/>Brotherhood Champion<br/>Brotherhood Chaplain<br/>Brotherhood Librarian<br/>Brotherhood Techmarine<br/>Brotherhood Terminator Squad<br/>Castellan Crowe<br/>Grand Master<br/>Grand Master In Nemesis Dreadknight<br/>Grand Master Voldus<br/>Interceptor Squad<br/>Kaldor Draigo<br/>Nemesis Dreadknight<br/>Paladin Squad<br/>Purgation Squad<br/>Purifier Squad<br/>Strike Squad<br/>Venerable Dreadnought</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Gate of Infinity</td><td><details><summary>20 units</summary>Brother-captain<br/>Brother-captain Stern<br/>Brotherhood Champion<br/>Brotherhood Chaplain<br/>Brotherhood Librarian<br/>Brotherhood Techmarine<br/>Brotherhood Terminator Squad<br/>Castellan Crowe<br/>Grand Master<br/>Grand Master In Nemesis Dreadknight<br/>Grand Master Voldus<br/>Grey Knights Dreadnought<br/>Interceptor Squad<br/>Kaldor Draigo<br/>Nemesis Dreadknight<br/>Paladin Squad<br/>Purgation Squad<br/>Purifier Squad<br/>Strike Squad<br/>Venerable Dreadnought</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is GREY KNIGHTS , at the end of your opponent&#x27;s Fight phase , you can select a number of units (see below) from your army that are on the battlefield (excluding units that are within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units), provided every model in those units has this ability. The maximum number of units you can select depends on the battle size, as follows: BATTLE SIZE NUMBER OF UNITS Incursion Up to 2 units Strike Force Up to 3 units Onslaught Up to 4 units Once you have made your selections, remove those units from the battlefield and place them into Strategic Reserves .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Teleport eligible units with placement validation.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Grey Knights Thunderhawk Gunship, Stormhawk Interceptor, Stormraven Gunship, Stormtalon Gunship</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>10 units</summary>Brother-captain<br/>Brother-captain Stern<br/>Brotherhood Champion<br/>Brotherhood Chaplain<br/>Brotherhood Librarian<br/>Brotherhood Techmarine<br/>Castellan Crowe<br/>Grand Master<br/>Grand Master Voldus<br/>Kaldor Draigo</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Strike Squad</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>
