### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Assigned Agents</td><td><details><summary>45 units</summary>Aquila Kill Team<br/>Callidus Assassin<br/>Corvus Blackstar<br/>Culexus Assassin<br/>Daemonhost<br/>Damned Legionnaires<br/>Deathwatch Kill Team<br/>Deathwatch Terminator Squad<br/>Eversor Assassin<br/>Exaction Squad<br/>Fortis Kill Team<br/>Grey Knights Terminator Squad<br/>Imperial Navy Breachers<br/>Imperial Rhino<br/>Indomitor Kill Team<br/>Inquisitor<br/>Inquisitor Coteaz<br/>Inquisitor Draxus<br/>Inquisitor Eisenhorn<br/>Inquisitor Greyfax<br/>Inquisitor In Terminator Armour<br/>Inquisitor Karamazov<br/>Inquisitor Ostromandeus<br/>Inquisitorial Agents<br/>Inquisitorial Chimera<br/>Janus Draik<br/>Jokaero Weaponsmith<br/>Kill Team Cassius<br/>Ministorum Priest<br/>Navigator<br/>Neyam Shai Murad<br/>Proteus Kill Team<br/>Rogue Trader Entourage<br/>Sanctifiers<br/>Sisters of Battle Immolator<br/>Sisters of Battle Squad<br/>Spectrus Kill Team<br/>Subductor Squad<br/>UR-025<br/>Veteran Bike Squad<br/>Vigilant Squad<br/>Vindicare Assassin<br/>Voidsmen-at-arms<br/>Watch Captain Artemis<br/>Watch Master</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is AGENTS OF THE IMPERIUM , then in the Select Detachment Rules step, you can select one of the available Detachments from this book as normal. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>7 units</summary>Callidus Assassin<br/>Culexus Assassin<br/>Damned Legionnaires<br/>Deathwatch Terminator Squad<br/>Grey Knights Terminator Squad<br/>Inquisitor In Terminator Armour<br/>Kill Team Cassius</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Inquisitor Eisenhorn, Inquisitor Ostromandeus, Watch Captain Artemis</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Callidus Assassin</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Imperial Rhino, Inquisitorial Chimera</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Corvus Blackstar</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Callidus Assassin<br/>Janus Draik<br/>Neyam Shai Murad<br/>Spectrus Kill Team<br/>Vindicare Assassin</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Kill Team</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Fortis Kill Team<br/>Indomitor Kill Team<br/>Kill Team Cassius<br/>Proteus Kill Team<br/>Spectrus Kill Team</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Each time an attack targets this unit, if it contains models with different Toughness characteristics, until the attacking unit has finished making its attacks, use the Toughness characteristic of the majority of the models in that unit when determining what roll is required for that attack to successfully wound. If two or more Toughness characteristics are tied for majority, use the highest value. For the purposes of determining which models in this unit can embark within a TRANSPORT , Kill Team Terminator models, Kill Team Outrider models, Kill Team Biker models and models equipped with a jump pack each take up the space of 2 models, but can otherwise embark within any TRANSPORT their unit can embark within, even though similar models in other units have the TERMINATOR , MOUNTED or JUMP PACK keywords . For the purposes of interacting with terrain features , all models in units with this ability are considered INFANTRY models, even though similar models in other units may have the MOUNTED or JUMP PACK keywords. Designer&#x27;s Note: While the abstractions in the above rule cause some models to behave differently to similar models in other units, they are designed to minimise complicated movement , TRANSPORT and Benefit of Cover rules.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No effect logic wired.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>15 units</summary>Inquisitor<br/>Inquisitor Coteaz<br/>Inquisitor Draxus<br/>Inquisitor Eisenhorn<br/>Inquisitor Greyfax<br/>Inquisitor In Terminator Armour<br/>Inquisitor Ostromandeus<br/>Janus Draik<br/>Jokaero Weaponsmith<br/>Ministorum Priest<br/>Navigator<br/>Neyam Shai Murad<br/>Rogue Trader Entourage<br/>Watch Captain Artemis<br/>Watch Master</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Callidus Assassin<br/>Culexus Assassin<br/>Eversor Assassin<br/>UR-025<br/>Vindicare Assassin</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Eversor Assassin, Sanctifiers, Spectrus Kill Team</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td>Corvus Blackstar, Culexus Assassin, Vindicare Assassin</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Imperial Knights (9 out of 17 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Code Chivalric</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is IMPERIAL KNIGHTS , at the end of the Read Mission Objectives step, you must determine your army&#x27;s Oath for the coming battle. An Oath consists of two parts - one Deed and one Quality. There are three options for each part, shown below. To determine your army&#x27;s Deed, you can either select one Deed or you can randomly select one Deed by rolling a D6 and consulting the relevant table below. The selected Deed will describe what needs to be achieved in order to complete that Deed. To determine your army&#x27;s Quality, you can either select one Quality or you can randomly select one Quality by rolling a D6 and consulting the relevant table below. Until the end of the battle, the ability described in the Quality selected applies to all models in your army with this ability. The first time your selected Deed is completed your Oath is fulfilled and, until the end of the battle, your army becomes Honoured and you gain 2CP, or 3CP if you randomly selected your Deed and/or Quality (CP gained in this way are an exemption to the Core Rules that limit the maximum number of CP you can gain per battle round to 1). Deed D6 We vow to lay low the tyrant... At the start of the battle, select one CHARACTER model in your opponent&#x27;s army. This Deed is completed at the end of a turn if that CHARACTER is destroyed. We swear to reclaim the realm... This deed is completed at the end of your opponent&#x27;s turn if you control more objective markers than your opponent. We pledge to reap a great tally... This deed is completed at the end of the battle round if the number of enemy units destroyed this battle round is greater than the battle round number even if those units are subsequently returned to the battlefield (for example, two destroyed enemy units in the first battle round). Quality D6 ...with our martial valour risen over all. Each time this model is selected to shoot or fight, you can re-roll one Hit roll and you can re-roll one Wound roll . ...and we are eager for the challenge. Add 2&quot; to this model&#x27;s Move characteristic and add 1 to Advance and Charge rolls made for this model. ...yet shall our legacy be unsullied. Improve this model&#x27;s Objective Control characteristic by 2 and its Leadership characteristic by 1.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Deed/Quality tracking with on-roll effects.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Bondsman</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Some IMPERIAL KNIGHTS models have a Bondsman ability, tagged with the word Bondsman&#x27;. In your Command phase , one or more models from your army with a Bondsman ability can use that ability. For each one that does, select one friendly ARMIGER model within 12&quot; of that model (you cannot select an ARMIGER model that is already being affected by a Bondsman ability). Until the start of your next Command phase, that ARMIGER model is affected by that Bondsman ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Bondsman buffs applied to Armiger units.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fff4cc"><td>Super-heavy Walker</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Each time a model with this ability makes a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move , it can move through models (excluding TITANIC models) and sections of terrain features that are 4&quot; or less in height. When doing so: - It can move within Engagement Range of enemy models, but cannot end that move within Engagement Range of them. - It can also move through sections of terrain features that are more than 4&quot; in height, but if it does, after it has moved, roll one D6: on a 1, that model is Battle-shocked .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Terrain traversal handling only.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Mustering Restrictions
<table><thead><tr><th>Restriction</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Freeblades</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Imperial Knights allies only; army must be IMPERIUM; allied Knights cannot be Warlord or take Enhancements; max 1 TITANIC or 3 ARMIGER, and cannot mix both.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Validated in Army._validate_freeblades.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Detachments
<details><summary>Gate Warden Lance</summary>
**Detachment Abilities**
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Dauntless Defenders</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> At the start of the first battle round , select two objective markers on the battlefield to be your foundations. When you draw a line from any part of one of your foundations to the other, if any part of a model&#x27;s base (or any part of a model&#x27;s hull, for a model without a base) crosses that line, that model&#x27;s unit is said to be on your defensive line. While an IMPERIAL KNIGHTS unit from your army is on your defensive line, that unit has the following ability: Against the Horde: Each time a model in this unit makes an attack that targets a visible enemy unit, you can ignore any or all modifiers to the Hit roll , and weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [sustained hits 1] ability. ### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Code Chivalric</td><td><details><summary>21 units</summary>Acastus Knight Asterius<br/>Acastus Knight Porphyrion<br/>Armiger Helverin<br/>Armiger Moirax<br/>Armiger Warglaive<br/>Canis Rex<br/>Cerastus Knight Acheron<br/>Cerastus Knight Atrapos<br/>Cerastus Knight Castigator<br/>Cerastus Knight Lancer<br/>Knight Castellan<br/>Knight Crusader<br/>Knight Defender<br/>Knight Errant<br/>Knight Gallant<br/>Knight Paladin<br/>Knight Preceptor<br/>Knight Valiant<br/>Knight Warden<br/>Questoris Knight Magaera<br/>Questoris Knight Styrix</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is IMPERIAL KNIGHTS , at the end of the Read Mission Objectives step, you must determine your army&#x27;s Oath for the coming battle. An Oath consists of two parts - one Deed and one Quality. There are three options for each part, shown below. To determine your army&#x27;s Deed, you can either select one Deed or you can randomly select one Deed by rolling a D6 and consulting the relevant table below. The selected Deed will describe what needs to be achieved in order to complete that Deed. To determine your army&#x27;s Quality, you can either select one Quality or you can randomly select one Quality by rolling a D6 and consulting the relevant table below. Until the end of the battle, the ability described in the Quality selected applies to all models in your army with this ability. The first time your selected Deed is completed your Oath is fulfilled and, until the end of the battle, your army becomes Honoured and you gain 2CP, or 3CP if you randomly selected your Deed and/or Quality (CP gained in this way are an exemption to the Core Rules that limit the maximum number of CP you can gain per battle round to 1). Deed D6 We vow to lay low the tyrant... At the start of the battle, select one CHARACTER model in your opponent&#x27;s army. This Deed is completed at the end of a turn if that CHARACTER is destroyed. We swear to reclaim the realm... This deed is completed at the end of your opponent&#x27;s turn if you control more objective markers than your opponent. We pledge to reap a great tally... This deed is completed at the end of the battle round if the number of enemy units destroyed this battle round is greater than the battle round number even if those units are subsequently returned to the battlefield (for example, two destroyed enemy units in the first battle round). Quality D6 ...with our martial valour risen over all. Each time this model is selected to shoot or fight, you can re-roll one Hit roll and you can re-roll one Wound roll . ...and we are eager for the challenge. Add 2&quot; to this model&#x27;s Move characteristic and add 1 to Advance and Charge rolls made for this model. ...yet shall our legacy be unsullied. Improve this model&#x27;s Objective Control characteristic by 2 and its Leadership characteristic by 1.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Deed/Quality tracking with on-roll effects.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>21 units</summary>Acastus Knight Asterius<br/>Acastus Knight Porphyrion<br/>Armiger Helverin<br/>Armiger Moirax<br/>Armiger Warglaive<br/>Canis Rex<br/>Cerastus Knight Acheron<br/>Cerastus Knight Atrapos<br/>Cerastus Knight Castigator<br/>Cerastus Knight Lancer<br/>Knight Castellan<br/>Knight Crusader<br/>Knight Defender<br/>Knight Errant<br/>Knight Gallant<br/>Knight Paladin<br/>Knight Preceptor<br/>Knight Valiant<br/>Knight Warden<br/>Questoris Knight Magaera<br/>Questoris Knight Styrix</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Doctrina Imperatives</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Skitarii Marshal<br/>Skitarii Rangers<br/>Skitarii Vanguard<br/>Tech-priest Dominus<br/>Tech-priest Manipulus</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> At the start of the battle round, you can select one of the Doctrina Imperatives below. Until the end of the battle round, that Doctrina Imperative is active for your army, and all units from your army that have the Doctrina Imperatives ability gain the relevant abilities shown below. Protector Imperative - Ranged weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [HEAVY] ability. - Improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of ranged weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1. - Each time a melee attack targets this unit, if this unit has the BATTLELINE keyword and/or it is within 6&quot; of one or more friendly ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE units, subtract 1 from the Hit roll . Conqueror Imperative - Ranged weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [ASSAULT] ability. - Improve the Weapon Skill characteristic of melee weapons equipped by models in this unit by 1. - Each time a model in this unit makes an attack, if this unit has the BATTLELINE keyword and/or it is within 6&quot; of one or more friendly ADEPTUS MECHANICUS BATTLELINE units, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 1.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Round-based imperatives with WS/BS/AP/heavy/assault modifiers.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td>Skitarii Marshal, Tech-priest Dominus, Tech-priest Manipulus</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Sir Hekhtur</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Skitarii Rangers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fff4cc"><td>Super-heavy Walker</td><td><details><summary>18 units</summary>Acastus Knight Asterius<br/>Acastus Knight Porphyrion<br/>Canis Rex<br/>Cerastus Knight Acheron<br/>Cerastus Knight Atrapos<br/>Cerastus Knight Castigator<br/>Cerastus Knight Lancer<br/>Knight Castellan<br/>Knight Crusader<br/>Knight Defender<br/>Knight Errant<br/>Knight Gallant<br/>Knight Paladin<br/>Knight Preceptor<br/>Knight Valiant<br/>Knight Warden<br/>Questoris Knight Magaera<br/>Questoris Knight Styrix</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Each time a model with this ability makes a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move , it can move through models (excluding TITANIC models) and sections of terrain features that are 4&quot; or less in height. When doing so: - It can move within Engagement Range of enemy models, but cannot end that move within Engagement Range of them. - It can also move through sections of terrain features that are more than 4&quot; in height, but if it does, after it has moved, roll one D6: on a 1, that model is Battle-shocked .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Terrain traversal handling only.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Aeldari (13 out of 24 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Battle Focus</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is ASURYANI , at the start of the battle round , you receive a number of Battle Focus tokens based on the battle size, as shown in the table below. BATTLE SIZE BATTLE FOCUS TOKENS Incursion 2 Strike Force 4 Onslaught 6 Each time one of the triggers shown in the Agile Manoeuvres section below occurs, you can spend one Battle Focus token to enable the relevant eligible unit to perform that Agile Manoeuvre. A unit is eligible to perform an Agile Manoeuvre if it has this ability and has not already performed an Agile Manoeuvre in the same phase. Unless otherwise stated, you cannot trigger the same Agile Manoeuvre more than once per phase. At the end of the battle round, all unspent Battle Focus tokens are lost. AGILE MANOEUVRES SWIFT AS THE WIND TRIGGER: When an eligible unit from your army is selected to make a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move . You can trigger this Agile Manoeuvre more than once per phase (provided a different unit performs it each time). EFFECT: Until the end of the phase, add 2&quot; to the Move characteristic of models in that unit. FLITTING SHADOWS TRIGGER: When an eligible unit from your army is selected to make a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move , is set up on the battlefield, or declares a charge . EFFECT: Until the end of the turn, enemy units cannot use the Fire Overwatch Stratagem to shoot at that unit. STAR ENGINES TRIGGER: When an eligible VEHICLE unit from your army is selected to make an Advance move . EFFECT: Until the end of the turn, Ranged weapons equipped by this unit have the [ASSAULT] ability. SUDDEN STRIKE TRIGGER: When an eligible unit from your army is selected to fight. EFFECT: Until the end of the phase, each time a model in that unit makes a Pile-in or Consolidation move , it can move up to 6&quot; instead of up to 3&quot;. OPPORTUNITY SEIZED TRIGGER: When an enemy unit ends a Fall Back move . EFFECT: One eligible unit from your army (excluding TITANIC units) that started the phase within Engagement Range of that enemy unit can make a Normal move of up to D6+1&quot;. FADE BACK TRIGGER: In your opponent&#x27;s Shooting phase , just after an enemy unit has shot. EFFECT: One eligible unit from your army (excluding TITANIC units) that was hit by one or more of those attacks can make a Normal move of up to D6+1&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Token system + maneuver selection with per-phase limits.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

In addition, at the end of your opponent&#x27;s turn, you can select a number of ASURYANI MOUNTED or VYPER units from your army (excluding units within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units), then remove those units from the battlefield and place them into Strategic Reserves. The maximum number of units you can select depends on the battle size, as shown below. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Amallyn Shadowguide, Death Jester, Solitaire</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Corsair Cloud Dancer Band<br/>Corsair Voidreavers<br/>Corsair Voidscarred<br/>Shroud Runners<br/>Striking Scorpions<br/>War Walkers</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>12 units</summary>Amallyn Shadowguide<br/>Illic Nightspear<br/>Irillyth<br/>Rangers<br/>Shadow Spectres<br/>Shadowseer<br/>Shroud Runners<br/>Solitaire<br/>Spiritseer<br/>Striking Scorpions<br/>Voidweaver<br/>Ynnari Venom</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Drukhari (13 out of 21 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#fff4cc"><td>Power from Pain</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Pain Abilities All DRUKHARI units have a Pain ability, tagged with the word Pain&#x27;. Pain abilities only apply to a unit while it is Empowered. If your Army Faction is DRUKHARI , you can Empower units from your army with Pain abilities by spending Pain tokens (see below). Designer&#x27;s Note: You can also spend Pain tokens to activate additional effects in certain other rules such as Enhancements and Stratagems. Gaining Pain Tokens If your Army Faction is DRUKHARI , you gain Pain tokens as follows: - 1 Pain token at the start of your Command phase . - 1 Pain token each time an enemy unit is destroyed. - 1 Pain token each time an enemy unit fails a Battle-shock test . Each time you gain a Pain token, keep it to one side - this is your Pain token pool. Each time you spend a Pain token, reduce your Pain token pool by the same amount. Empowered Through Pain Each Pain ability will state when you can spend Pain tokens to Empower that unit. When you do, until the end of the phase, that unit is Empowered and all Pain abilities it has take effect. While an Attached unit is Empowered, the Pain abilities of all Leader and Bodyguard units in that unit take effect - you do not need to spend additional Pain tokens to activate each of those Pain abilities. Example: At the start of your Charge phase , you spend 1 Pain token to Empower a unit of Wyches . The unit becomes Empowered, and so its Acrobatic Gladiators ability takes effect until the end of the phase. A Succubus is leading the unit, and so its Lithe Agility ability also takes effect until the end of the phase (no additional Pain token is required to activate that ability as well).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pain token engine with partial ability coverage.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Battle Focus</td><td><details><summary>10 units</summary>Corsair Voidreavers<br/>Corsair Voidscarred<br/>Death Jester<br/>Shadowseer<br/>Skyweavers<br/>Solitaire<br/>Starweaver<br/>Troupe<br/>Troupe Master<br/>Voidweaver</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is ASURYANI , at the start of the battle round , you receive a number of Battle Focus tokens based on the battle size, as shown in the table below. BATTLE SIZE BATTLE FOCUS TOKENS Incursion 2 Strike Force 4 Onslaught 6 Each time one of the triggers shown in the Agile Manoeuvres section below occurs, you can spend one Battle Focus token to enable the relevant eligible unit to perform that Agile Manoeuvre. A unit is eligible to perform an Agile Manoeuvre if it has this ability and has not already performed an Agile Manoeuvre in the same phase. Unless otherwise stated, you cannot trigger the same Agile Manoeuvre more than once per phase. At the end of the battle round, all unspent Battle Focus tokens are lost. AGILE MANOEUVRES SWIFT AS THE WIND TRIGGER: When an eligible unit from your army is selected to make a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move . You can trigger this Agile Manoeuvre more than once per phase (provided a different unit performs it each time). EFFECT: Until the end of the phase, add 2&quot; to the Move characteristic of models in that unit. FLITTING SHADOWS TRIGGER: When an eligible unit from your army is selected to make a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move , is set up on the battlefield, or declares a charge . EFFECT: Until the end of the turn, enemy units cannot use the Fire Overwatch Stratagem to shoot at that unit. STAR ENGINES TRIGGER: When an eligible VEHICLE unit from your army is selected to make an Advance move . EFFECT: Until the end of the turn, Ranged weapons equipped by this unit have the [ASSAULT] ability. SUDDEN STRIKE TRIGGER: When an eligible unit from your army is selected to fight. EFFECT: Until the end of the phase, each time a model in that unit makes a Pile-in or Consolidation move , it can move up to 6&quot; instead of up to 3&quot;. OPPORTUNITY SEIZED TRIGGER: When an enemy unit ends a Fall Back move . EFFECT: One eligible unit from your army (excluding TITANIC units) that started the phase within Engagement Range of that enemy unit can make a Normal move of up to D6+1&quot;. FADE BACK TRIGGER: In your opponent&#x27;s Shooting phase , just after an enemy unit has shot. EFFECT: One eligible unit from your army (excluding TITANIC units) that was hit by one or more of those attacks can make a Normal move of up to D6+1&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Token system + maneuver selection with per-phase limits.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>12 units</summary>Cronos<br/>Raider<br/>Ravager<br/>Raven Strike Fighter<br/>Razorwing Jetfighter<br/>Reaper<br/>Starweaver<br/>Talos<br/>Tantalus<br/>Venom<br/>Voidraven Bomber<br/>Voidweaver</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>10 units</summary>Corsair Skyreaver Band<br/>Hellions<br/>Mandrakes<br/>Raider<br/>Ravager<br/>Reaper<br/>Scourges with Heavy Weapons<br/>Scourges with Shardcarbines<br/>Tantalus<br/>Venom</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Disparate Paths</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Death Jester<br/>Shadowseer<br/>Skyweavers<br/>Solitaire<br/>Starweaver<br/>Troupe<br/>Troupe Master<br/>Voidweaver</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> When mustering your army, you can include HARLEQUINS units in your army, even though they do not have the ASURYANI Faction keyword . Unless otherwise stated, you cannot select HARLEQUINS or YNNARI as your Army Faction.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Harlequin/Ynnari ally validation in mustering.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Cronos<br/>Grotesques<br/>Haemonculus<br/>Lady Malys<br/>Talos<br/>Urien Rakarth</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Lelith Hesperax, Solitaire</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Raider, Starweaver, Tantalus, Venom</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Mandrakes</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>9 units</summary>Archon<br/>Drazhar<br/>Haemonculus<br/>Lady Malys<br/>Lelith Hesperax<br/>Shadowseer<br/>Succubus<br/>Troupe Master<br/>Urien Rakarth</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Death Jester, Solitaire</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fff4cc"><td>Power from Pain</td><td><details><summary>30 units</summary>Archon<br/>Beastmaster<br/>Court of the Archon<br/>Cronos<br/>Drazhar<br/>Grotesques<br/>Haemonculus<br/>Hand of the Archon<br/>Hellions<br/>Incubi<br/>Kabalite Warriors<br/>Lady Malys<br/>Lelith Hesperax<br/>Mandrakes<br/>Raider<br/>Ravager<br/>Raven Strike Fighter<br/>Razorwing Jetfighter<br/>Reaper<br/>Reavers<br/>Scourges with Heavy Weapons<br/>Scourges with Shardcarbines<br/>Succubus<br/>Talos<br/>Tantalus<br/>Urien Rakarth<br/>Venom<br/>Voidraven Bomber<br/>Wracks<br/>Wyches</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Pain Abilities All DRUKHARI units have a Pain ability, tagged with the word Pain&#x27;. Pain abilities only apply to a unit while it is Empowered. If your Army Faction is DRUKHARI , you can Empower units from your army with Pain abilities by spending Pain tokens (see below). Designer&#x27;s Note: You can also spend Pain tokens to activate additional effects in certain other rules such as Enhancements and Stratagems. Gaining Pain Tokens If your Army Faction is DRUKHARI , you gain Pain tokens as follows: - 1 Pain token at the start of your Command phase . - 1 Pain token each time an enemy unit is destroyed. - 1 Pain token each time an enemy unit fails a Battle-shock test . Each time you gain a Pain token, keep it to one side - this is your Pain token pool. Each time you spend a Pain token, reduce your Pain token pool by the same amount. Empowered Through Pain Each Pain ability will state when you can spend Pain tokens to Empower that unit. When you do, until the end of the phase, that unit is Empowered and all Pain abilities it has take effect. While an Attached unit is Empowered, the Pain abilities of all Leader and Bodyguard units in that unit take effect - you do not need to spend additional Pain tokens to activate each of those Pain abilities. Example: At the start of your Charge phase , you spend 1 Pain token to Empower a unit of Wyches . The unit becomes Empowered, and so its Acrobatic Gladiators ability takes effect until the end of the phase. A Succubus is leading the unit, and so its Lithe Agility ability also takes effect until the end of the phase (no additional Pain token is required to activate that ability as well).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pain token engine with partial ability coverage.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Beastmaster<br/>Corsair Cloud Dancer Band<br/>Corsair Voidreavers<br/>Corsair Voidscarred<br/>Hand of the Archon</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Mandrakes<br/>Raven Strike Fighter<br/>Razorwing Jetfighter<br/>Shadowseer<br/>Solitaire<br/>Venom<br/>Voidraven Bomber<br/>Voidweaver</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Cult Ambush</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is GENESTEALER CULTS , you start the battle with a number of Resurgence points, depending on the battle size, as shown below. - Incursion: 6 Resurgence points - Strike Force: 10 Resurgence points - Onslaught: 14 Resurgence points Each time a unit from your army is destroyed, if every model in that unit has this ability, you can spend the relevant number of Resurgence points shown below based on that unit&#x27;s Starting Strength . Aberrants 5 models 4 Resurgence points 10 models 8 Resurgence points Acolyte Hybrids with Autopistols , Acolyte Hybrids with Hand Flamers , Hybrid Metamorphs 5 models 2 Resurgence points 10 models 4 Resurgence points Atalan Jackals 5 models 2 Resurgence points 10 models 6 Resurgence points Neophyte Hybrids 10 models 3 Resurgence points 20 models 6 Resurgence points Purestrain Genestealers 5 models 2 Resurgence points 10 models 6 Resurgence points If you do: - Add a new unit to your army identical to your destroyed unit, in Cult Ambush, at its Starting Strength, with all of its wounds remaining and any [ONE SHOT] weapons those models are equipped with considered as not having been shot. - Place one Cult Ambush marker (see below) anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy units (if this is not possible, no marker is placed). Units in Cult Ambush Cult Ambush is a type of Strategic Reserves . Units in Cult Ambush cannot be targeted with the Rapid Ingress Stratagem, but can be set up on the battlefield using a Cult Ambush marker as described below, or by following the rules for Strategic Reserves in a subsequent turn. Cult Ambush Markers Use a circular 32mm diameter marker for Cult Ambush markers. If an enemy model (excluding AIRCRAFT ) ends any kind of move within 9&quot; of a Cult Ambush marker you placed, that Cult Ambush marker is removed from the battlefield. At the end of the Reinforcements step of your opponent&#x27;s next Movement phase , for each of your Cult Ambush markers still on the battlefield, you can select one unit from your army that is in Cult Ambush and set up that unit using that Cult Ambush marker. To do so, set that unit up on the battlefield more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy units, with at least one model in that unit touching that Cult Ambush marker and all other models placed wholly within 3&quot; of that Cult Ambush marker (that Cult Ambush marker is then removed from the battlefield).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Resurgence points, ambush markers, reinforcements.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Cult Ambush</td><td><details><summary>7 units</summary>Aberrants<br/>Acolyte Hybrids With Autopistols<br/>Acolyte Hybrids With Hand Flamers<br/>Atalan Jackals<br/>Hybrid Metamorphs<br/>Neophyte Hybrids<br/>Purestrain Genestealers</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is GENESTEALER CULTS , you start the battle with a number of Resurgence points, depending on the battle size, as shown below. - Incursion: 6 Resurgence points - Strike Force: 10 Resurgence points - Onslaught: 14 Resurgence points Each time a unit from your army is destroyed, if every model in that unit has this ability, you can spend the relevant number of Resurgence points shown below based on that unit&#x27;s Starting Strength . Aberrants 5 models 4 Resurgence points 10 models 8 Resurgence points Acolyte Hybrids with Autopistols , Acolyte Hybrids with Hand Flamers , Hybrid Metamorphs 5 models 2 Resurgence points 10 models 4 Resurgence points Atalan Jackals 5 models 2 Resurgence points 10 models 6 Resurgence points Neophyte Hybrids 10 models 3 Resurgence points 20 models 6 Resurgence points Purestrain Genestealers 5 models 2 Resurgence points 10 models 6 Resurgence points If you do: - Add a new unit to your army identical to your destroyed unit, in Cult Ambush, at its Starting Strength, with all of its wounds remaining and any [ONE SHOT] weapons those models are equipped with considered as not having been shot. - Place one Cult Ambush marker (see below) anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy units (if this is not possible, no marker is placed). Units in Cult Ambush Cult Ambush is a type of Strategic Reserves . Units in Cult Ambush cannot be targeted with the Rapid Ingress Stratagem, but can be set up on the battlefield using a Cult Ambush marker as described below, or by following the rules for Strategic Reserves in a subsequent turn. Cult Ambush Markers Use a circular 32mm diameter marker for Cult Ambush markers. If an enemy model (excluding AIRCRAFT ) ends any kind of move within 9&quot; of a Cult Ambush marker you placed, that Cult Ambush marker is removed from the battlefield. At the end of the Reinforcements step of your opponent&#x27;s next Movement phase , for each of your Cult Ambush markers still on the battlefield, you can select one unit from your army that is in Cult Ambush and set up that unit using that Cult Ambush marker. To do so, set that unit up on the battlefield more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy units, with at least one model in that unit touching that Cult Ambush marker and all other models placed wholly within 3&quot; of that Cult Ambush marker (that Cult Ambush marker is then removed from the battlefield).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Resurgence points, ambush markers, reinforcements.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>71 units</summary>Achilles Ridgerunners<br/>Arkurian Stormhammer<br/>Armageddon-pattern Medusa<br/>Armoured Sentinels<br/>Atlas Recovery Vehicle<br/>Baneblade<br/>Banehammer<br/>Banesword<br/>Basilisk<br/>Carnodon<br/>Centaur Light Carrier<br/>Chimera<br/>Colossus<br/>Crassus<br/>Cyclops Demolition Vehicle<br/>Deathstrike<br/>Dominus Armoured Siege Bombard<br/>Doomhammer<br/>Earthshaker Platform<br/>Elysian Drop Sentinel<br/>Goliath Rockgrinder<br/>Goliath Truck<br/>Gorgon Heavy Transport<br/>Griffon Mortar Carrier<br/>Hellhammer<br/>Hellhound<br/>Hydra<br/>Hydra Platform<br/>Leman Russ Battle Tank<br/>Leman Russ Commander<br/>Leman Russ Demolisher<br/>Leman Russ Eradicator<br/>Leman Russ Executioner<br/>Leman Russ Exterminator<br/>Leman Russ Punisher<br/>Leman Russ Vanquisher<br/>Macharius<br/>Macharius Omega<br/>Macharius Vanquisher<br/>Macharius Vulcan<br/>Malcador<br/>Malcador Annihilator<br/>Malcador Defender<br/>Malcador Infernus<br/>Manticore<br/>Manticore Platform<br/>Minotaur<br/>Praetor<br/>Rogal Dorn Battle Tank<br/>Rogal Dorn Commander<br/>Salamander Command Vehicle<br/>Salamander Scout Vehicle<br/>Scout Sentinels<br/>Sentinel Powerlifter<br/>Shadowsword<br/>Storm Chimera<br/>Stormblade<br/>Stormlord<br/>Stormsword<br/>Stygies Destroyer Tank Hunter<br/>Tarantula Battery<br/>Tauros Assault Vehicle<br/>Tauros Venator<br/>Taurox<br/>Taurox Prime<br/>Tectonic Fragdrill<br/>Trojan Support Vehicle<br/>Tyrannocyte<br/>Valdor<br/>Winged Hive Tyrant<br/>Wyvern</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>31 units</summary>Aberrants<br/>Abominant<br/>Acolyte Hybrids With Autopistols<br/>Acolyte Hybrids With Hand Flamers<br/>Acolyte Iconward<br/>Benefictus<br/>Biophagus<br/>Clamavus<br/>Elysian Drop Sentinel<br/>Elysian Sniper Squad<br/>Gargoyles<br/>Hades Breaching Drill<br/>Hybrid Metamorphs<br/>Hyperadapted Raveners<br/>Kelermorph<br/>Locus<br/>Magus<br/>Mawloc<br/>Neophyte Hybrids<br/>Nexos<br/>Parasite Of Mortrex<br/>Patriarch<br/>Primus<br/>Purestrain Genestealers<br/>Raveners<br/>Reductus Saboteur<br/>Sanctus<br/>Trygon<br/>Tyrannocyte<br/>Winged Hive Tyrant<br/>Winged Tyranid Prime</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Aberrants, Abominant, Hybrid Metamorphs</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds.
