Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Deathleaper, Lictor, Locus, Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td><details><summary>7 units</summary>Banehammer<br/>Chimera<br/>Doomhammer<br/>Goliath Rockgrinder<br/>Goliath Truck<br/>Storm Chimera<br/>Stormlord</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Deathleaper<br/>Lictor<br/>Neurolictor<br/>Patriarch<br/>Purestrain Genestealers<br/>Reductus Saboteur<br/>Sanctus<br/>Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>21 units</summary>Abominant<br/>Acolyte Iconward<br/>Benefictus<br/>Biophagus<br/>Cadian Castellan<br/>Cadian Command Squad<br/>Catachan Command Squad<br/>Clamavus<br/>Death Rider Commissar<br/>Hell&#x27;s Last<br/>Hyperadapted Raveners<br/>Jackal Alphus<br/>Krieg Command Squad<br/>Locus<br/>Magus<br/>Nexos<br/>Patriarch<br/>Primaris Psyker<br/>Primus<br/>Quartermaster Cadre Squad<br/>Winged Tyranid Prime</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td><details><summary>7 units</summary>Deathleaper<br/>Kelermorph<br/>Lictor<br/>Neurolictor<br/>Parasite Of Mortrex<br/>Reductus Saboteur<br/>Sanctus</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td><details><summary>14 units</summary>Achilles Ridgerunners<br/>Acolyte Iconward<br/>Atalan Jackals<br/>Catachan Command Squad<br/>Catachan Heavy Weapons Squad<br/>Catachan Jungle Fighters<br/>Hybrid Metamorphs<br/>Jackal Alphus<br/>Kasrkin<br/>Krieg Combat Engineers<br/>Mukaali Riders<br/>Salamander Scout Vehicle<br/>Scout Sentinels<br/>Tauros Assault Vehicle</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Shadow in the Warp</td><td>Hyperadapted Raveners, Neurolictor, Winged Hive Tyrant, Winged Tyranid Prime</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is TYRANIDS , once per battle, in either player&#x27;s Command phase , if one or more units from your army with this ability are on the battlefield, you can unleash the Shadow in the Warp. When you do, each enemy unit on the battlefield must take a Battle-shock test . Each time an enemy unit takes such a Battle-shock test, if it is within 6&quot; of one or more SYNAPSE units from your army, subtract 1 from that test.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Once-per-battle armywide Battle-shock trigger.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>9 units</summary>Atalan Jackals<br/>Deathleaper<br/>Jackal Alphus<br/>Lictor<br/>Neurolictor<br/>Parasite Of Mortrex<br/>Reductus Saboteur<br/>Sanctus<br/>Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Synapse</td><td><details><summary>13 units</summary>Deathleaper<br/>Gargoyles<br/>Hyperadapted Raveners<br/>Lictor<br/>Mawloc<br/>Neurolictor<br/>Parasite Of Mortrex<br/>Raveners<br/>Trygon<br/>Tyrannocyte<br/>Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers<br/>Winged Hive Tyrant<br/>Winged Tyranid Prime</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is TYRANIDS , while a TYRANIDS unit from your army is within 6&quot; of one or more friendly SYNAPSE models, that TYRANIDS unit is said to be within Synapse Range of that model and of your army. While a TYRANIDS unit from your army is within Synapse Range of your army: - Each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test , take that test on 3D6 instead of 2D6. - Each time a model in that unit makes a melee attack, add 1 to the Strength characteristic of that attack.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Synapse aura checks via distance rules.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Leagues of Votann (11 out of 16 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Prioritised Efficiency</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is LEAGUES OF VOTANN , LEAGUES OF VOTANN units from your army have one of two abilities: Hostile Acquisition or Fortify Takeover (see below). During the battle, which ability those LEAGUES OF VOTANN units have will change depending on how many Yield points (YP) you currently have: - At the start of the battle, your units have Hostile Acquisition until the start of your next Command phase . - At the end of your Command phase, if you have fewer than 7YP, your units have Hostile Acquisition until the start of your next Command phase. - At the end of your Command phase, if you have 7YP or more, your units have Fortify Takeover until the start of your next Command phase. Hostile Acquisition - Each time a model in this unit makes an attack that targets an enemy unit within range of one or more objective markers , add 1 to the Hit roll . - You can re-roll Advance and Charge rolls made for this unit. Fortify Takeover - Each time a model in this unit makes an attack that targets an enemy unit, if this unit is within range of one or more objective markers you control, add 1 to the Hit roll. - Each time an attack targets this unit, if the Strength characteristic of that attack is greater than this unit&#x27;s Toughness characteristic and this unit is not a VEHICLE , subtract 1 from the Wound roll . Yield Points At the end of each player&#x27;s Command phase, you gain 1YP if you control one or more objective markers within your deployment zone, and, from the second battle round onwards, you gain 1 additional YP for each of the following conditions you satisfy: - You control one or more objective markers not within your deployment zone. - You control two or more objective markers not within your deployment zone. - You control more objective markers than your opponent. In your turn, YP gained in this way are always gained before checking which ability LEAGUES OF VOTANN units from your army have. Whenever a rule allows you to spend YP, reduce the number of YP you have by that amount (your YP cannot go below 0), otherwise you cannot use that rule. Designer&#x27;s Note: This means you can use rules that let you gain or spend YP to influence which ability your units have - Hostile Acquisition or Fortify Takeover - depending on which will be most beneficial to you. Remember that your army only changes ability at the end of your Command phase, so you will - sometimes need to plan ahead if you want your army to stay in or change ability. Example: In her third turn, Freida&#x27;s units had the Hostile Acquisition ability, as she had 6YP at the end of her Command phase. In her fourth turn, at the end of her Command phase, she controls one objective marker within her deployment zone, and one objective marker not within her deployment zone, and her opponent controls two objective markers. Freida gains 2YP, so she now has 8YP, and her units now have the Fortify Takeover ability instead. During her turn, Freida uses a Stratagem that allows her to spend YP. She spends 2YP, bringing her total down to 6YP. However, units from her army still have Fortify Takeover - it will only change if, at the end of her next Command phase, she still has fewer than 7YP.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Yield points + mode tracking with objective checks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Arkanyst Evaluator<br/>Hekaton Land Fortress<br/>Kapricus Carrier<br/>Kapricus Defenders<br/>Sagitaur</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Cthonian Beserks, Hearthkyn Warriors</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Kapricus Carrier</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Hernkyn Yaegirs</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Brkhyr Iron-master<br/>Einhyr Champion<br/>Grimnyr<br/>Khl<br/>Memnyr Strategist<br/>thar the Destined</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Buri Aegnirssen</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Prioritised Efficiency</td><td><details><summary>21 units</summary>Arkanyst Evaluator<br/>Brkhyr Iron-master<br/>Brkhyr Thunderkyn<br/>Buri Aegnirssen<br/>Cthonian Beserks<br/>Cthonian Earthshakers<br/>Einhyr Champion<br/>Einhyr Hearthguard<br/>Grimnyr<br/>Hearthkyn Warriors<br/>Hekaton Land Fortress<br/>Hernkyn Pioneers<br/>Hernkyn Yaegirs<br/>Ironkin Steeljacks with Heavy Volkanite Disintegrators<br/>Ironkin Steeljacks with Melee Weapons<br/>Kapricus Carrier<br/>Kapricus Defenders<br/>Khl<br/>Memnyr Strategist<br/>Sagitaur<br/>thar the Destined</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is LEAGUES OF VOTANN , LEAGUES OF VOTANN units from your army have one of two abilities: Hostile Acquisition or Fortify Takeover (see below). During the battle, which ability those LEAGUES OF VOTANN units have will change depending on how many Yield points (YP) you currently have: - At the start of the battle, your units have Hostile Acquisition until the start of your next Command phase . - At the end of your Command phase, if you have fewer than 7YP, your units have Hostile Acquisition until the start of your next Command phase. - At the end of your Command phase, if you have 7YP or more, your units have Fortify Takeover until the start of your next Command phase. Hostile Acquisition - Each time a model in this unit makes an attack that targets an enemy unit within range of one or more objective markers , add 1 to the Hit roll . - You can re-roll Advance and Charge rolls made for this unit. Fortify Takeover - Each time a model in this unit makes an attack that targets an enemy unit, if this unit is within range of one or more objective markers you control, add 1 to the Hit roll. - Each time an attack targets this unit, if the Strength characteristic of that attack is greater than this unit&#x27;s Toughness characteristic and this unit is not a VEHICLE , subtract 1 from the Wound roll . Yield Points At the end of each player&#x27;s Command phase, you gain 1YP if you control one or more objective markers within your deployment zone, and, from the second battle round onwards, you gain 1 additional YP for each of the following conditions you satisfy: - You control one or more objective markers not within your deployment zone. - You control two or more objective markers not within your deployment zone. - You control more objective markers than your opponent. In your turn, YP gained in this way are always gained before checking which ability LEAGUES OF VOTANN units from your army have. Whenever a rule allows you to spend YP, reduce the number of YP you have by that amount (your YP cannot go below 0), otherwise you cannot use that rule. Designer&#x27;s Note: This means you can use rules that let you gain or spend YP to influence which ability your units have - Hostile Acquisition or Fortify Takeover - depending on which will be most beneficial to you. Remember that your army only changes ability at the end of your Command phase, so you will - sometimes need to plan ahead if you want your army to stay in or change ability. Example: In her third turn, Freida&#x27;s units had the Hostile Acquisition ability, as she had 6YP at the end of her Command phase. In her fourth turn, at the end of her Command phase, she controls one objective marker within her deployment zone, and one objective marker not within her deployment zone, and her opponent controls two objective markers. Freida gains 2YP, so she now has 8YP, and her units now have the Fortify Takeover ability instead. During her turn, Freida uses a Stratagem that allows her to spend YP. She spends 2YP, bringing her total down to 6YP. However, units from her army still have Fortify Takeover - it will only change if, at the end of her next Command phase, she still has fewer than 7YP.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Yield points + mode tracking with objective checks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Hernkyn Pioneers, Kapricus Carrier, Kapricus Defenders</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td>Buri Aegnirssen</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Necrons (11 out of 21 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Reanimation Protocols</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is NECRONS , at the end of your Command phase , each unit from your army with this ability that is on the battlefield activates its Reanimation Protocols and reanimates D3 wounds. Each time such a unit reanimates a wound: - If that unit contains one or more models with fewer than their starting number of wounds remaining, select one of those models; that model regains one lost wound - If all models in that unit have their starting number of wounds, but that unit is not at its Starting Strength , one destroyed model is returned to that unit with one wound remaining. Once such a unit is at its Starting Strength and all of its models have their starting number of wounds, nothing further happens. Example: A unit of Lokhust Destroyers (which have a Wounds characteristic of 3) activates its Reanimation Protocols. The unit had a Starting Strength of 3, but currently contains 2 models, and one of those models has lost 1 wound. A 3 is rolled to see how many wounds are reanimated. The first of these reanimated wounds restores the wounded Lokhust Destroyer back to 3 wounds. The second of these reanimated wounds returns the destroyed Lokhust Destroyer to the battlefield with 1 wound remaining. The third of these reanimated wounds restores one of the remaining lost wounds to the same Lokhust Destroyer that was just returned. The unit now contains 3 models, two of which have 3 wounds remaining and one of which has 2 wounds remaining.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Command-phase reanimation sequencing for Necrons.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>23 units</summary>Annihilation Barge<br/>Canoptek Doomstalker<br/>Canoptek Spyders<br/>Catacomb Command Barge<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Deceiver<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Nightbringer<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Void Dragon<br/>Doom Scythe<br/>Doomsday Ark<br/>Gauss Pylon<br/>Ghost Ark<br/>Monolith<br/>Night Scythe<br/>Night Shroud<br/>Obelisk<br/>Sentry Pylon<br/>Seraptek Heavy Construct<br/>Tesseract Ark<br/>Tesseract Vault<br/>The Silent King<br/>Tomb Citadel Walls<br/>Transcendent C&#x27;tan<br/>Triarch Stalker</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>14 units</summary>Canoptek Tomb Sentinel<br/>Canoptek Tomb Stalker<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Deceiver<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Nightbringer<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Void Dragon<br/>Deathmarks<br/>Hexmark Destroyer<br/>Monolith<br/>Nekrosor Ammentar<br/>Night Scythe<br/>Obelisk<br/>Ophydian Destroyers<br/>Transcendent C&#x27;tan<br/>Triarch Praetorians</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Canoptek Reanimator<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Deceiver<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Nightbringer<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Void Dragon<br/>Illuminor Szeras<br/>Transcendent C&#x27;tan</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Nekrosor Ammentar</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Canoptek Acanthrites, Flayed Ones</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>17 units</summary>Anrakyr The Traveller<br/>Chronomancer<br/>Geomancer<br/>Imotekh The Stormlord<br/>Lokhust Lord<br/>Lord<br/>Nemesor Zahndrekh<br/>Orikan The Diviner<br/>Overlord<br/>Overlord with translocation shroud<br/>Plasmancer<br/>Psychomancer<br/>Royal Warden<br/>Skorpekh Lord<br/>Technomancer<br/>Trazyn The Infinite<br/>Vargard Obyron</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Hexmark Destroyer</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Reanimation Protocols</td><td><details><summary>64 units</summary>Annihilation Barge<br/>Anrakyr The Traveller<br/>Canoptek Acanthrites<br/>Canoptek Doomstalker<br/>Canoptek Macrocytes<br/>Canoptek Reanimator<br/>Canoptek Scarab Swarms<br/>Canoptek Spyders<br/>Canoptek Tomb Crawlers<br/>Canoptek Tomb Sentinel<br/>Canoptek Tomb Stalker<br/>Canoptek Wraiths<br/>Catacomb Command Barge<br/>Chronomancer<br/>Convergence Of Dominion<br/>Cryptothralls<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Deceiver<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Nightbringer<br/>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Void Dragon<br/>Deathmarks<br/>Doom Scythe<br/>Doomsday Ark<br/>Flayed Ones<br/>Gauss Pylon<br/>Geomancer<br/>Ghost Ark<br/>Hexmark Destroyer<br/>Illuminor Szeras<br/>Immortals<br/>Imotekh The Stormlord<br/>Lokhust Destroyers<br/>Lokhust Heavy Destroyers<br/>Lokhust Lord<br/>Lord<br/>Lychguard<br/>Monolith<br/>Necron Warriors<br/>Nekrosor Ammentar<br/>Nemesor Zahndrekh<br/>Night Scythe<br/>Night Shroud<br/>Obelisk<br/>Ophydian Destroyers<br/>Orikan The Diviner<br/>Overlord<br/>Overlord with translocation shroud<br/>Plasmancer<br/>Psychomancer<br/>Royal Warden<br/>Sentry Pylon<br/>Seraptek Heavy Construct<br/>Skorpekh Destroyers<br/>Skorpekh Lord<br/>Technomancer<br/>Tesseract Ark<br/>Tesseract Vault<br/>The Silent King<br/>Tomb Blades<br/>Tomb Citadel Walls<br/>Transcendent C&#x27;tan<br/>Trazyn The Infinite<br/>Triarch Praetorians<br/>Triarch Stalker<br/>Vargard Obyron</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is NECRONS , at the end of your Command phase , each unit from your army with this ability that is on the battlefield activates its Reanimation Protocols and reanimates D3 wounds. Each time such a unit reanimates a wound: - If that unit contains one or more models with fewer than their starting number of wounds remaining, select one of those models; that model regains one lost wound - If all models in that unit have their starting number of wounds, but that unit is not at its Starting Strength , one destroyed model is returned to that unit with one wound remaining. Once such a unit is at its Starting Strength and all of its models have their starting number of wounds, nothing further happens. Example: A unit of Lokhust Destroyers (which have a Wounds characteristic of 3) activates its Reanimation Protocols. The unit had a Starting Strength of 3, but currently contains 2 models, and one of those models has lost 1 wound. A 3 is rolled to see how many wounds are reanimated. The first of these reanimated wounds restores the wounded Lokhust Destroyer back to 3 wounds. The second of these reanimated wounds returns the destroyed Lokhust Destroyer to the battlefield with 1 wound remaining. The third of these reanimated wounds restores one of the remaining lost wounds to the same Lokhust Destroyer that was just returned. The unit now contains 3 models, two of which have 3 wounds remaining and one of which has 2 wounds remaining.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Command-phase reanimation sequencing for Necrons.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Canoptek Macrocytes, Tomb Blades, Triarch Stalker</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td>C&#x27;tan Shard of the Deceiver, Flayed Ones</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>39 units</summary>Attack Fighta<br/>Battlewagon<br/>Big Trakk<br/>Big&#x27;ed Bossbunka<br/>Blitza-bommer<br/>Boomdakka Snazzwagon<br/>Burna-bommer<br/>Chinork Warkopta<br/>Da Red Gobbo&#x27;s Tinboy<br/>Dakkajet<br/>Deff Dread<br/>Deff Rolla Battle Fortress<br/>Deffkilla Wartrike<br/>Fighta-bommer<br/>Gargantuan Squiggoth<br/>Gorkanaut<br/>Grot Mega-tank<br/>Grot Tanks<br/>Hunta Rig<br/>Kannonwagon<br/>Kill Krusha<br/>Kill Rig<br/>Kill Tank<br/>Killa Kans<br/>Kustom Boosta-blasta<br/>Lifta Wagon<br/>Mega Dread<br/>Megatrakk Scrapjet<br/>Meka-dread<br/>Mekboy Workshop<br/>Morkanaut<br/>Rukkatrukk Squigbuggy<br/>Shokkjump Dragsta<br/>Squiggoth<br/>Stompa<br/>Trukk<br/>Wazbom Blastajet<br/>Weirdboy<br/>Wurrboy</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Boss Zagstruk<br/>Chinork Warkopta<br/>Deffkoptas<br/>Deffkoptas With Big Shootas<br/>Stormboyz</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>12 units</summary>Beast Snagga Boyz<br/>Beastboss<br/>Beastboss On Squigosaur<br/>Boss Zagstruk<br/>Hunta Rig<br/>Kill Rig<br/>Mad Dok Grotsnik<br/>Mozrog Skragbad<br/>Painboss<br/>Squighog Boyz<br/>Wurrboy<br/>Zodgrod Wortsnagga</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td><details><summary>11 units</summary>Battlewagon<br/>Big Trakk<br/>Big&#x27;ed Bossbunka<br/>Chinork Warkopta<br/>Deff Rolla Battle Fortress<br/>Gargantuan Squiggoth<br/>Hunta Rig<br/>Kannonwagon<br/>Kill Krusha<br/>Squiggoth<br/>Trukk</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Boss Snikrot, Kommandos</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>27 units</summary>Beastboss<br/>Beastboss On Squigosaur<br/>Big Mek<br/>Big Mek In Mega Armour<br/>Big Mek On Warbike<br/>Big Mek With Kustom Force Field<br/>Big Mek With Shokk Attack Gun<br/>Boss Snikrot<br/>Boss Zagstruk<br/>Da Red Gobbo<br/>Deffkilla Wartrike<br/>Ghazghkull Thraka<br/>Kaptin Badrukk<br/>Mad Dok Grotsnik<br/>Mek<br/>Mozrog Skragbad<br/>Nob With Waaagh! Banner<br/>Painboss<br/>Painboy<br/>Painboy On Warbike<br/>Ufthak Blackhawk<br/>Warboss<br/>Warboss In Mega Armour<br/>Warboss On Warbike<br/>Weirdboy<br/>Wurrboy<br/>Zodgrod Wortsnagga</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Boss Snikrot, Da Red Gobbo&#x27;s Tinboy</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Da Red Gobbo&#x27;s Tinboy</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td>Boss Snikrot, Kommandos</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Waaagh!</td><td><details><summary>86 units</summary>Attack Fighta<br/>Battlewagon<br/>Beast Snagga Boyz<br/>Beastboss<br/>Beastboss On Squigosaur<br/>Big Gunz<br/>Big Mek<br/>Big Mek In Mega Armour<br/>Big Mek On Warbike<br/>Big Mek With Kustom Force Field<br/>Big Mek With Shokk Attack Gun<br/>Big Trakk<br/>Big&#x27;ed Bossbunka<br/>Blitza-bommer<br/>Boomdakka Snazzwagon<br/>Boss Snikrot<br/>Boss Zagstruk<br/>Boyz<br/>Breaka Boyz<br/>Burna Boyz<br/>Burna-bommer<br/>Chinork Warkopta<br/>Da Red Gobbo<br/>Da Red Gobbo&#x27;s Tinboy<br/>Dakkajet<br/>Deff Dread<br/>Deff Rolla Battle Fortress<br/>Deffkilla Wartrike<br/>Deffkoptas<br/>Deffkoptas With Big Shootas<br/>Fighta-bommer<br/>Flash Gitz<br/>Gargantuan Squiggoth<br/>Ghazghkull Thraka<br/>Gorkanaut<br/>Gretchin<br/>Grot Bomm Launcha<br/>Grot Mega-tank<br/>Grot Tanks<br/>Hunta Rig<br/>Kannonwagon<br/>Kaptin Badrukk<br/>Kill Krusha<br/>Kill Rig<br/>Kill Tank<br/>Killa Kans<br/>Kommandos<br/>Kustom Boosta-blasta<br/>Lifta Wagon<br/>Lootas<br/>Mad Dok Grotsnik<br/>Mega Dread<br/>Meganobz<br/>Megatrakk Scrapjet<br/>Mek<br/>Mek Gunz<br/>Meka-dread<br/>Mekboy Workshop<br/>Morkanaut<br/>Mozrog Skragbad<br/>Nob With Waaagh! During your Shooting phase, for each Observer unit from your army that has not been selected to shoot this phase and is eligible to shoot (excluding FORTIFICATION and Battle-shocked units) select one enemy unit that is visible to be marked as their Spotted unit until the end of the phase. Each enemy unit can only be marked as a Spotted unit once per phase. Units from your army with the For the Greater Good ability (excluding Observer units) are Guided units while targeting one or more Spotted units. Until the end of the phase, each time a model from your army in a Guided unit makes an attack that targets a Spotted unit, improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of that attack by 1 and, if the Spotted unit was marked by an Observer unit that has the MARKERLIGHT keyword, that attack has the [IGNORES COVER] ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Observer/Guided targeting with markerlight bonuses.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>
