### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>23 units</summary>AX-1-0 Tiger Shark<br/>Barracuda<br/>Devilfish<br/>Ghostkeel Battlesuit<br/>Hammerhead Gunship<br/>Longstrike<br/>Manta<br/>Orca Dropship<br/>Piranhas<br/>Razorshark Strike Fighter<br/>Riptide Battlesuit<br/>R&#x27;varna Battlesuit<br/>Sky Ray Gunship<br/>Stormsurge<br/>Sun Shark Bomber<br/>Ta&#x27;unar Supremacy Armour<br/>Tetras<br/>Tidewall Droneport<br/>Tidewall Gunrig<br/>Tidewall Shieldline<br/>Tiger Shark<br/>Tx42 Piranha<br/>Y&#x27;vahra Battlesuit</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>12 units</summary>Commander Farsight<br/>Commander In Coldstar Battlesuit<br/>Commander In Crisis Battlesuit<br/>Commander In Enforcer Battlesuit<br/>Crisis Battlesuits<br/>Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits<br/>Crisis Starscythe Battlesuits<br/>Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits<br/>Shas&#x27;o R&#x27;alai<br/>Tactical Drones<br/>Vespid Stingwings<br/>Xv9 Hazard Battlesuits</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Tidewall Droneport, Tidewall Gunrig, Tidewall Shieldline</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>For the Greater Good</td><td><details><summary>41 units</summary>AX-1-0 Tiger Shark<br/>Barracuda<br/>Breacher Team<br/>Broadside Battlesuits<br/>Cadre Fireblade<br/>Commander Farsight<br/>Commander In Coldstar Battlesuit<br/>Commander In Crisis Battlesuit<br/>Commander In Enforcer Battlesuit<br/>Commander Shadowsun<br/>Crisis Battlesuits<br/>Crisis Fireknife Battlesuits<br/>Crisis Starscythe Battlesuits<br/>Crisis Sunforge Battlesuits<br/>Darkstrider<br/>Devilfish<br/>Ethereal<br/>Firesight Team<br/>Ghostkeel Battlesuit<br/>Hammerhead Gunship<br/>Longstrike<br/>Manta<br/>Orca Dropship<br/>Pathfinder Team<br/>Piranhas<br/>Razorshark Strike Fighter<br/>Remora Stealth Drones<br/>Riptide Battlesuit<br/>R&#x27;varna Battlesuit<br/>Shas&#x27;o R&#x27;alai<br/>Sky Ray Gunship<br/>Stealth Battlesuits<br/>Stormsurge<br/>Strike Team<br/>Sun Shark Bomber<br/>Ta&#x27;unar Supremacy Armour<br/>Tetras<br/>Tiger Shark<br/>Tx42 Piranha<br/>Xv9 Hazard Battlesuits<br/>Y&#x27;vahra Battlesuit</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is T&#x27;AU EMPIRE , at the start of your Shooting phase you can select units from your army with this ability to become Observer units. During your Shooting phase, for each Observer unit from your army that has not been selected to shoot this phase and is eligible to shoot (excluding FORTIFICATION and Battle-shocked units) select one enemy unit that is visible to be marked as their Spotted unit until the end of the phase. Each enemy unit can only be marked as a Spotted unit once per phase. Units from your army with the For the Greater Good ability (excluding Observer units) are Guided units while targeting one or more Spotted units. Until the end of the phase, each time a model from your army in a Guided unit makes an attack that targets a Spotted unit, improve the Ballistic Skill characteristic of that attack by 1 and, if the Spotted unit was marked by an Observer unit that has the MARKERLIGHT keyword, that attack has the [IGNORES COVER] ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Observer/Guided targeting with markerlight bonuses.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Manta, Orca Dropship</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td><details><summary>11 units</summary>Commander Shadowsun<br/>Darkstrider<br/>Firesight Team<br/>Ghostkeel Battlesuit<br/>Kroot Farstalkers<br/>Kroot Flesh Shaper<br/>Kroot Trail Shaper<br/>Kroot War Shaper<br/>Remora Stealth Drones<br/>Stealth Battlesuits<br/>Tetras</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>12 units</summary>Aun&#x27;shi<br/>Cadre Fireblade<br/>Commander Farsight<br/>Commander In Coldstar Battlesuit<br/>Commander In Crisis Battlesuit<br/>Commander In Enforcer Battlesuit<br/>Darkstrider<br/>Ethereal<br/>Kroot Flesh Shaper<br/>Kroot Trail Shaper<br/>Kroot War Shaper<br/>Shas&#x27;o R&#x27;alai</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Aun&#x27;va<br/>Commander Shadowsun<br/>Firesight Team<br/>Ghostkeel Battlesuit<br/>Kroot Lone-Spear</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td><details><summary>14 units</summary>Darkstrider<br/>Great Knarloc<br/>Knarloc Riders<br/>Kroot Carnivores<br/>Kroot Flesh Shaper<br/>Kroot Hounds<br/>Kroot Lone-Spear<br/>Kroot Trail Shaper<br/>Kroot War Shaper<br/>Krootox Rampagers<br/>Krootox Riders<br/>Pathfinder Team<br/>Piranhas<br/>Tx42 Piranha</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>13 units</summary>Commander Shadowsun<br/>Firesight Team<br/>Ghostkeel Battlesuit<br/>Knarloc Riders<br/>Kroot Carnivores<br/>Kroot Farstalkers<br/>Kroot Flesh Shaper<br/>Kroot Hounds<br/>Kroot Lone-Spear<br/>Kroot Trail Shaper<br/>Kroot War Shaper<br/>Remora Stealth Drones<br/>Stealth Battlesuits</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

While a TYRANIDS unit from your army is within Synapse Range of your army: - Each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test , take that test on 3D6 instead of 2D6. - Each time a model in that unit makes a melee attack, add 1 to the Strength characteristic of that attack.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Synapse aura checks via distance rules.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Shadow in the Warp</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is TYRANIDS , once per battle, in either player&#x27;s Command phase , if one or more units from your army with this ability are on the battlefield, you can unleash the Shadow in the Warp. Each time an enemy unit takes such a Battle-shock test, if it is within 6&quot; of one or more SYNAPSE units from your army, subtract 1 from that test.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Once-per-battle armywide Battle-shock trigger.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>25 units</summary>Barbed Hierodule<br/>Biovores<br/>Carnifexes<br/>Dimachaeron<br/>Exocrine<br/>Harpy<br/>Harridan<br/>Haruspex<br/>Hierophant<br/>Hive Crone<br/>Hive Tyrant<br/>Maleceptor<br/>Norn Assimilator<br/>Norn Emissary<br/>Psychophage<br/>Pyrovores<br/>Screamer-killer<br/>Scythed Hierodule<br/>Sporocyst<br/>Tervigon<br/>The Swarmlord<br/>Toxicrene<br/>Tyrannocyte<br/>Tyrannofex<br/>Winged Hive Tyrant</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>13 units</summary>Gargoyles<br/>Hyperadapted Raveners<br/>Mawloc<br/>Mucolid Spores<br/>Parasite Of Mortrex<br/>Raveners<br/>Ripper Swarms<br/>Sky-slasher Swarms<br/>Spore Mines<br/>Trygon<br/>Tyrannocyte<br/>Winged Hive Tyrant<br/>Winged Tyranid Prime</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Old One Eye, Psychophage</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Deathleaper, Lictor, Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Harpy, Harridan, Hive Crone</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Deathleaper, Lictor, Neurolictor, Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Broodlord<br/>Hive Tyrant<br/>Hyperadapted Raveners<br/>Malanthrope<br/>Neurotyrant<br/>Old One Eye<br/>The Swarmlord<br/>Winged Tyranid Prime</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Deathleaper, Lictor, Neurolictor, Parasite Of Mortrex</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Broodlord, Genestealers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Shadow in the Warp</td><td><details><summary>16 units</summary>Broodlord<br/>Hive Tyrant<br/>Hyperadapted Raveners<br/>Malanthrope<br/>Maleceptor<br/>Neurolictor<br/>Neurotyrant<br/>Norn Assimilator<br/>Norn Emissary<br/>Tervigon<br/>The Swarmlord<br/>Tyranid Warriors With Melee Bio-weapons<br/>Tyranid Warriors With Ranged Bio-weapons<br/>Winged Hive Tyrant<br/>Winged Tyranid Prime<br/>Zoanthropes</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is TYRANIDS , once per battle, in either player&#x27;s Command phase , if one or more units from your army with this ability are on the battlefield, you can unleash the Shadow in the Warp. When you do, each enemy unit on the battlefield must take a Battle-shock test . Each time an enemy unit takes such a Battle-shock test, if it is within 6&quot; of one or more SYNAPSE units from your army, subtract 1 from that test.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Once-per-battle armywide Battle-shock trigger.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>7 units</summary>Deathleaper<br/>Lictor<br/>Malanthrope<br/>Neurolictor<br/>Parasite Of Mortrex<br/>Venomthropes<br/>Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Synapse</td><td><details><summary>55 units</summary>Barbed Hierodule<br/>Barbgaunts<br/>Biovores<br/>Broodlord<br/>Carnifexes<br/>Deathleaper<br/>Dimachaeron<br/>Exocrine<br/>Gargoyles<br/>Genestealers<br/>Harpy<br/>Harridan<br/>Haruspex<br/>Hierophant<br/>Hive Crone<br/>Hive Guard<br/>Hive Tyrant<br/>Hormagaunts<br/>Hyperadapted Raveners<br/>Lictor<br/>Malanthrope<br/>Maleceptor<br/>Mawloc<br/>Mucolid Spores<br/>Neurogaunts<br/>Neurolictor<br/>Neurotyrant<br/>Norn Assimilator<br/>Norn Emissary<br/>Old One Eye<br/>Parasite Of Mortrex<br/>Psychophage<br/>Pyrovores<br/>Raveners<br/>Ripper Swarms<br/>Screamer-killer<br/>Scythed Hierodule<br/>Sky-slasher Swarms<br/>Spore Mines<br/>Sporocyst<br/>Termagants<br/>Tervigon<br/>The Swarmlord<br/>Toxicrene<br/>Trygon<br/>Tyranid Warriors With Melee Bio-weapons<br/>Tyranid Warriors With Ranged Bio-weapons<br/>Tyrannocyte<br/>Tyrannofex<br/>Tyrant Guard<br/>Venomthropes<br/>Von Ryan&#x27;s Leapers<br/>Winged Hive Tyrant<br/>Winged Tyranid Prime<br/>Zoanthropes</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is TYRANIDS , while a TYRANIDS unit from your army is within 6&quot; of one or more friendly SYNAPSE models, that TYRANIDS unit is said to be within Synapse Range of that model and of your army. While a TYRANIDS unit from your army is within Synapse Range of your army: - Each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test , take that test on 3D6 instead of 2D6. - Each time a model in that unit makes a melee attack, add 1 to the Strength characteristic of that attack.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Synapse aura checks via distance rules.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Chaos Daemons (13 out of 22 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>The Shadow of Chaos</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is LEGIONES DAEMONICA , certain areas of the battlefield are considered to be within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos, as follows: - Your deployment zone is always within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos. - At the start of any phase, if you control at least half of the objective markers within No Man&#x27;s Land, until the end of that phase, No Man&#x27;s Land is within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos. - At the start of any phase, if you control at least half of the objective markers within your opponent&#x27;s deployment zone, until the end of that phase, your opponent&#x27;s deployment zone is within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos. DAEMONIC MANIFESTATION While a LEGIONES DAEMONICA unit from your army is within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos, each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test , add 1 to that test and, if that test is passed, one model in that unit regains up to D3 lost wounds (if that unit is a BATTLELINE unit and that test is passed, up to D3 destroyed models can be returned to that unit instead). DAEMONIC TERROR While an enemy unit is within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos and/or it is within 6&quot; of one or more BLOODTHIRSTER , GREAT UNCLEAN ONE , KAIROS FATEWEAVER , KEEPER OF SECRETS , LORD OF CHANGE , ROTIGUS , SHALAXI HELBANE or SKARBRAND units from your army, each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test , subtract 1 from that test and, if that test is failed, that enemy unit suffers D3 mortal wounds .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Shadow zones + manifestations/terror handling.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Mustering Restrictions
<table><thead><tr><th>Restriction</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Daemonic Pact</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEGIONES DAEMONICA allies allowed only in CSM/Chaos Knights; allies cannot be Warlord or take Enhancements; points cap enforced and god non-Battleline cannot exceed Battleline.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Validated in Army._validate_daemonic_pact.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

**Detachment Abilities**
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Fates in Flux</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> You start the battle with three Flux tokens (we recommend using a dice to track how many Flux tokens you have). In your Command phase , if your opponent has one or more Flux tokens, you gain one Flux token. Designer&#x27;s Note: When using fast dice rolling , this rule can be used to spend any number of Flux tokens (up to the amount you have), to re-roll a number of dice up to the amount spent, after rolling multiple rolls or saving throws at once.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No effect logic wired.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>The Blue Scribes, The Changeling, The Masque Of Slaanesh</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Accursed Cultists, Beasts Of Nurgle, Herald Of Slaanesh On Steed Of Slaanesh, Seekers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td>Be&#x27;lakor, The Changeling</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. At the start of any phase, if you control at least half of the objective markers within your opponent&#x27;s deployment zone, until the end of that phase, your opponent&#x27;s deployment zone is within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos. DAEMONIC MANIFESTATION While a LEGIONES DAEMONICA unit from your army is within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos, each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test , add 1 to that test and, if that test is passed, one model in that unit regains up to D3 lost wounds (if that unit is a BATTLELINE unit and that test is passed, up to D3 destroyed models can be returned to that unit instead). DAEMONIC TERROR While an enemy unit is within your army&#x27;s Shadow of Chaos and/or it is within 6&quot; of one or more BLOODTHIRSTER , GREAT UNCLEAN ONE , KAIROS FATEWEAVER , KEEPER OF SECRETS , LORD OF CHANGE , ROTIGUS , SHALAXI HELBANE or SKARBRAND units from your army, each time that unit takes a Battle-shock test , subtract 1 from that test and, if that test is failed, that enemy unit suffers D3 mortal wounds .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Shadow zones + manifestations/terror handling.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Chaos Knights (8 out of 15 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Harbingers of Dread</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is CHAOS KNIGHTS , each unit from your army with this ability gains Dread abilities, depending which are active for your army (see below). The Deathly Terror ability is active for your army from the start of the battle. In addition, at the start of the first, third and fifth battle rounds , you can either select one of the other Dread abilities or randomly select two Dread abilities to apply by rolling two D6 and applying the results rolled, from those numbered 1-6. Any Dread abilities that have been selected are active until the end of the battle. You cannot select the same Dread ability more than once, and any duplicated Dread abilities (as a result of randomly selecting them) have no additional effect. DEATHLY TERROR (AURA) N/A While an enemy unit is within 9&quot; of this model, worsen the Leadership characteristic of models in that unit by 1. DESPAIR (AURA) While an enemy unit is within 9&quot; of this model, worsen the Leadership characteristic of models in that unit by 1. This is cumulative with the Deathly Terror ability (see above). DOOM Each time this model makes an attack, if the target of that attack is Battle-shocked , add 1 to the Wound roll . DARKNESS Each time an attack is made against this model, if the attacking unit is Battle-shocked or more than 18&quot; away, subtract 1 from the Hit roll . DISMAY (AURA) In the Battle-shock step of your opponent&#x27;s Command phase , for each enemy unit that is below its Starting Strength and within 9&quot; of this model, that enemy unit must take a Battle-shock test. DELIRIUM (AURA) While an enemy unit that is Below Half-strength is within 9&quot; of this model, each time that unit fails a Battle-shock test , it suffers D3 mortal wounds . DOMINION Add 3&quot; to the range of this model&#x27;s Aura abilities .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Dread ability selection and aura checks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fff4cc"><td>Super-heavy Walker</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Each time a model with this ability makes a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move , it can move through models (excluding TITANIC models) and sections of terrain features that are 4&quot; or less in height. When doing so: - It can move within Engagement Range of enemy models, but cannot end that move within Engagement Range of them. - It can also move through sections of terrain features that are more than 4&quot; in height, but if it does, after it has moved, roll one D6: on a 1, that model is Battle-shocked .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Terrain traversal handling only.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Dark Pacts</td><td><details><summary>17 units</summary>Accursed Cultists<br/>Cultist Firebrand<br/>Cultist Mob<br/>Cultist Mob with Firearms<br/>Dark Commune<br/>Fellgor Beastmen<br/>Gellerpox Infected<br/>Mutoid Vermin<br/>Negavolt Cultists<br/>Renegade Enforcer<br/>Renegade Heavy Weapons Squad<br/>Renegade Ogryn Beast Handler<br/>Renegade Ogryn Brutes<br/>Renegade Plague Ogryns<br/>Rogue Psyker<br/>Traitor Enforcer<br/>Traitor Guardsmen Squad</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is HERETIC ASTARTES , each time a unit with this ability is selected to shoot or fight, it can make a Dark Pact. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Accursed Cultists<br/>Gellerpox Infected<br/>Mutoid Vermin<br/>Negavolt Cultists<br/>Renegade Plague Ogryns</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Harbingers of Dread</td><td><details><summary>20 units</summary>Chaos Acastus Knight Asterius<br/>Chaos Acastus Knight Porphyrion<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Acheron<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Castigator<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Lancer<br/>Chaos Questoris Knight Magaera<br/>Chaos Questoris Knight Styrix<br/>Knight Abominant<br/>Knight Desecrator<br/>Knight Despoiler<br/>Knight Rampager<br/>Knight Ruinator<br/>Knight Tyrant<br/>War Dog Brigand<br/>War Dog Executioner<br/>War Dog Huntsman<br/>War Dog Karnivore<br/>War Dog Moirax<br/>War Dog Stalker</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is CHAOS KNIGHTS , each unit from your army with this ability gains Dread abilities, depending which are active for your army (see below). The Deathly Terror ability is active for your army from the start of the battle. In addition, at the start of the first, third and fifth battle rounds , you can either select one of the other Dread abilities or randomly select two Dread abilities to apply by rolling two D6 and applying the results rolled, from those numbered 1-6. Any Dread abilities that have been selected are active until the end of the battle. You cannot select the same Dread ability more than once, and any duplicated Dread abilities (as a result of randomly selecting them) have no additional effect. DEATHLY TERROR (AURA) N/A While an enemy unit is within 9&quot; of this model, worsen the Leadership characteristic of models in that unit by 1. DESPAIR (AURA) While an enemy unit is within 9&quot; of this model, worsen the Leadership characteristic of models in that unit by 1. This is cumulative with the Deathly Terror ability (see above). DOOM Each time this model makes an attack, if the target of that attack is Battle-shocked , add 1 to the Wound roll . DARKNESS Each time an attack is made against this model, if the attacking unit is Battle-shocked or more than 18&quot; away, subtract 1 from the Hit roll . DISMAY (AURA) In the Battle-shock step of your opponent&#x27;s Command phase , for each enemy unit that is below its Starting Strength and within 9&quot; of this model, that enemy unit must take a Battle-shock test. DELIRIUM (AURA) While an enemy unit that is Below Half-strength is within 9&quot; of this model, each time that unit fails a Battle-shock test , it suffers D3 mortal wounds . DOMINION Add 3&quot; to the range of this model&#x27;s Aura abilities .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Dread ability selection and aura checks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Cultist Firebrand<br/>Dark Commune<br/>Renegade Enforcer<br/>Rogue Psyker<br/>Traitor Enforcer</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Accursed Cultists, War Dog Stalker</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fff4cc"><td>Super-heavy Walker</td><td><details><summary>14 units</summary>Chaos Acastus Knight Asterius<br/>Chaos Acastus Knight Porphyrion<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Acheron<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Atrapos<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Castigator<br/>Chaos Cerastus Knight Lancer<br/>Chaos Questoris Knight Magaera<br/>Chaos Questoris Knight Styrix<br/>Knight Abominant<br/>Knight Desecrator<br/>Knight Despoiler<br/>Knight Rampager<br/>Knight Ruinator<br/>Knight Tyrant</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> Each time a model with this ability makes a Normal , Advance or Fall Back move , it can move through models (excluding TITANIC models) and sections of terrain features that are 4&quot; or less in height. When doing so: - It can move within Engagement Range of enemy models, but cannot end that move within Engagement Range of them. - It can also move through sections of terrain features that are more than 4&quot; in height, but if it does, after it has moved, roll one D6: on a 1, that model is Battle-shocked .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Terrain traversal handling only.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

Each Blessing of Khorne specifies the dice results it requires (where a number is specified, a double or triple of that value or higher is required). If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>7 units</summary>Accursed Cultists<br/>Chaos Spawn<br/>Fabius Bile<br/>Gellerpox Infected<br/>Mutoid Vermin<br/>Negavolt Cultists<br/>Renegade Plague Ogryns</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Chaos Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Chaos Thunderhawk<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Heldrake<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>28 units</summary>Abaddon The Despoiler<br/>Chaos Lord<br/>Chaos Lord In Terminator Armour<br/>Chaos Lord On Bike<br/>Chaos Lord On Disc Of Tzeentch<br/>Chaos Lord On Juggernaut<br/>Chaos Lord On Palanquin Of Nurgle<br/>Chaos Lord On Steed Of Slaanesh<br/>Chaos Lord with Jump Pack<br/>Cultist Firebrand<br/>Dark Apostle<br/>Dark Commune<br/>Exalted Champion<br/>Fabius Bile<br/>Haarken Worldclaimer<br/>Huron Blackheart<br/>Master Of Executions<br/>Master Of Possession<br/>Renegade Enforcer<br/>Rogue Psyker<br/>Sorcerer<br/>Sorcerer In Terminator Armour<br/>Sorcerer On Bike<br/>Sorcerer On Disc Of Tzeentch<br/>Sorcerer On Palanquin Of Nurgle<br/>Sorcerer On Steed Of Slaanesh<br/>Traitor Enforcer<br/>Warpsmith</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Cypher</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Nurgle&#x27;s Gift (Aura)</td><td>Plague Marines</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is DEATH GUARD , while an enemy unit is within Contagion Range of one or more DEATH GUARD models from your army, it is Afflicted (see below). CONTAGION RANGE Contagion Range changes over the course of the battle: AFFLICTED During the Declare Battle Formations step, select one of the Plagues below. Until the end of the battle, while an enemy unit is Afflicted, subtract 1 from the Toughness characteristic of models in that unit, and that unit has the effect of your chosen Plague. Skullsquirm Blight This horrifying affliction sees the minds and senses of the victim gnawed gradually away from within. Each time a model in this unit makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll . Rattlejoint Ague Limbs shuddering with fever palsy, bones turned brittle as glass, these warriors can barely act to defend themselves. Worsen the Save characteristic of models in this unit by 1. Scabrous Soulrot Victims of this insidious ailment become glassy eyed and morose as their very animus and essence decay. Worsen the Move, Leadership, and Objective Control characteristics of models in this unit by 1 (this rule can only worsen a model&#x27;s Objective Control characteristic to a minimum of 1).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Contagion range + plague effects.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Accursed Cultists</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td>Nemesis Claw</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Thrill Seekers</td><td>Noise Marines</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is EMPEROR&#x27;S CHILDREN , this unit is eligible to shoot and declare a charge in a turn in which it Advanced or Fell Back , but when doing so: - It cannot target a unit it was within Engagement Range of at the start of the turn. - It cannot target a unit that was the target of another units charge or attack this phase.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> EC core rule hooks for crits and movement bonuses.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>44 units</summary>Beasts of Nurgle<br/>Biologus Putrifier<br/>Cerberus<br/>Chaos Land Raider<br/>Chaos Predator Annihilator<br/>Chaos Predator Destructor<br/>Chaos Rhino<br/>Chaos Spawn<br/>Chaos Thunderhawk<br/>Daemon Prince of Nurgle<br/>Daemon Prince of Nurgle with Wings<br/>Defiler<br/>Deredeo Dreadnought<br/>Falchion<br/>Fellblade<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Foetid Bloat-drone<br/>Foetid Bloat-drone with Heavy Blight Launcher<br/>Great Unclean One<br/>Greater Blight Drone<br/>Helbrute<br/>Hell Blade<br/>Hell Talon<br/>Kratos<br/>Land Raider Achilles<br/>Land Raider Proteus<br/>Leviathan Dreadnought<br/>Mastodon<br/>Miasmic Malignifier<br/>Mortarion<br/>Myphitic Blight-hauler<br/>Plagueburst Crawler<br/>Relic Contemptor Dreadnought<br/>Rotigus<br/>Sicaran Battle Tank<br/>Sicaran Punisher<br/>Sicaran Venator<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Spartan<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite<br/>Typhon<br/>Whirlwind Scorpius<br/>Xiphon Interceptor</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat.
