When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>17 units</summary>Beasts of Nurgle<br/>Blightlord Terminators<br/>Daemon Prince of Nurgle with Wings<br/>Death Guard Chaos Lord In Terminator Armour<br/>Death Guard Sorcerer In Terminator Armour<br/>Deathshroud Terminators<br/>Great Unclean One<br/>Greater Blight Drone<br/>Lord of Contagion<br/>Lord of Virulence<br/>Mortarion<br/>Nurglings<br/>Plague Drones<br/>Plaguebearers<br/>Rotigus<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite<br/>Typhus</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td><details><summary>7 units</summary>Chaos Spawn<br/>Gellerpox Infected<br/>Great Unclean One<br/>Mortarion<br/>Mutoid Vermin<br/>Poxwalkers<br/>Rotigus</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Chaos Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Chaos Thunderhawk, Fire Raptor Gunship, Sokar-pattern Stormbird, Storm Eagle Gunship</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Nurglings, Poxwalkers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>16 units</summary>Biologus Putrifier<br/>Chaos Lord On Palanquin Of Nurgle<br/>Death Guard Chaos Lord<br/>Death Guard Chaos Lord In Terminator Armour<br/>Death Guard Sorcerer In Terminator Armour<br/>Foul Blightspawn<br/>Icon Bearer<br/>Lord of Contagion<br/>Lord of Poxes<br/>Lord of Virulence<br/>Malignant Plaguecaster<br/>Noxious Blightbringer<br/>Plague Surgeon<br/>Sorcerer On Palanquin Of Nurgle<br/>Tallyman<br/>Typhus</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Nurgle&#x27;s Gift (Aura)</td><td><details><summary>65 units</summary>Biologus Putrifier<br/>Blightlord Terminators<br/>Cerberus<br/>Chaos Land Raider<br/>Chaos Lord On Palanquin Of Nurgle<br/>Chaos Predator Annihilator<br/>Chaos Predator Destructor<br/>Chaos Rhino<br/>Chaos Spawn<br/>Chaos Thunderhawk<br/>Daemon Prince of Nurgle<br/>Daemon Prince of Nurgle with Wings<br/>Death Guard Chaos Lord<br/>Death Guard Chaos Lord In Terminator Armour<br/>Death Guard Cultists<br/>Death Guard Possessed<br/>Death Guard Sorcerer In Terminator Armour<br/>Deathshroud Terminators<br/>Defiler<br/>Deredeo Dreadnought<br/>Falchion<br/>Fellblade<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Foetid Bloat-drone<br/>Foetid Bloat-drone with Heavy Blight Launcher<br/>Foul Blightspawn<br/>Gellerpox Infected<br/>Greater Blight Drone<br/>Helbrute<br/>Hell Blade<br/>Hell Talon<br/>Icon Bearer<br/>Kratos<br/>Land Raider Achilles<br/>Land Raider Proteus<br/>Leviathan Dreadnought<br/>Lord of Contagion<br/>Lord of Poxes<br/>Lord of Virulence<br/>Malignant Plaguecaster<br/>Mastodon<br/>Miasmic Malignifier<br/>Mortarion<br/>Mutoid Vermin<br/>Myphitic Blight-hauler<br/>Noxious Blightbringer<br/>Plague Marines<br/>Plague Surgeon<br/>Plagueburst Crawler<br/>Poxwalkers<br/>Rapier Carrier<br/>Relic Contemptor Dreadnought<br/>Sicaran Battle Tank<br/>Sicaran Punisher<br/>Sicaran Venator<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Sorcerer On Palanquin Of Nurgle<br/>Spartan<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship<br/>Tallyman<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite<br/>Typhon<br/>Typhus<br/>Whirlwind Scorpius<br/>Xiphon Interceptor</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is DEATH GUARD , while an enemy unit is within Contagion Range of one or more DEATH GUARD models from your army, it is Afflicted (see below). CONTAGION RANGE Contagion Range changes over the course of the battle: AFFLICTED During the Declare Battle Formations step, select one of the Plagues below. Until the end of the battle, while an enemy unit is Afflicted, subtract 1 from the Toughness characteristic of models in that unit, and that unit has the effect of your chosen Plague. Skullsquirm Blight This horrifying affliction sees the minds and senses of the victim gnawed gradually away from within. Each time a model in this unit makes an attack, subtract 1 from the Hit roll . Rattlejoint Ague Limbs shuddering with fever palsy, bones turned brittle as glass, these warriors can barely act to defend themselves. Worsen the Save characteristic of models in this unit by 1. Scabrous Soulrot Victims of this insidious ailment become glassy eyed and morose as their very animus and essence decay. Worsen the Move, Leadership, and Objective Control characteristics of models in this unit by 1 (this rule can only worsen a model&#x27;s Objective Control characteristic to a minimum of 1).<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Contagion range + plague effects.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Pact of Decay</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Beasts of Nurgle<br/>Great Unclean One<br/>Nurglings<br/>Plague Drones<br/>Plaguebearers<br/>Rotigus</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> When mustering your army, unless specifically stated otherwise, you cannot select PLAGUE LEGIONS as your Army Faction .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Army faction restriction enforced during validation.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Beasts of Nurgle, Chaos Spawn, Death Guard Cultists</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>9 units</summary>Chaos Land Raider<br/>Chaos Rhino<br/>Daemon Prince of Slaanesh<br/>Daemon Prince of Slaanesh with Wings<br/>Fulgrim<br/>Heldrake<br/>Keeper of Secrets<br/>Maulerfiend<br/>Shalaxi Helbane</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Chaos Terminators<br/>Daemon Prince of Slaanesh with Wings<br/>Daemonettes<br/>Fiends<br/>Fulgrim<br/>Keeper of Secrets<br/>Seekers<br/>Shalaxi Helbane</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Chaos Spawn, Lucius the Eternal</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Daemonettes</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Units with this ability that are eligible to fight do so in the Fights First step, provided every model in the unit has this ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Fight phase sequencing uses Fights First step.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Chaos Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td>Heldrake</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Tormentors</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td>Lord Exultant, Lord Kakophonist, Lucius the Eternal, Sorcerer</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td>Lucius the Eternal</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Unless part of an Attached unit (see Leader ), this unit can only be selected as the target of a ranged attack if the attacking model is within 12&quot;.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Ranged targeting blocked beyond 12&quot; when not Attached.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Pact of Excess</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Daemonettes<br/>Fiends<br/>Keeper of Secrets<br/>Seekers<br/>Shalaxi Helbane</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> When mustering your army, unless specifically stated otherwise, you cannot select LEGIONS OF EXCESS as your Army Faction.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Army faction restriction enforced during validation.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Infractors, Seekers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Thrill Seekers</td><td><details><summary>17 units</summary>Chaos Land Raider<br/>Chaos Rhino<br/>Chaos Spawn<br/>Chaos Terminators<br/>Daemon Prince of Slaanesh<br/>Daemon Prince of Slaanesh with Wings<br/>Flawless Blades<br/>Fulgrim<br/>Heldrake<br/>Infractors<br/>Lord Exultant<br/>Lord Kakophonist<br/>Lucius the Eternal<br/>Maulerfiend<br/>Noise Marines<br/>Sorcerer<br/>Tormentors</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is EMPEROR&#x27;S CHILDREN , this unit is eligible to shoot and declare a charge in a turn in which it Advanced or Fell Back , but when doing so: - It cannot target a unit it was within Engagement Range of at the start of the turn. - It cannot target a unit that was the target of another units charge or attack this phase.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> EC core rule hooks for crits and movement bonuses.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">Thousand Sons (12 out of 20 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Cabal of Sorcerers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is THOUSAND SONS , at the start of your Shooting phase , one or more models from your army with this ability can attempt Rituals from those listed below. To do so, select one model from your army with this ability that has not yet attempted a Ritual this turn and select one Ritual no model from your army has attempted to manifest this turn, then take a Psychic test for that model by following the sequence below. PSYCHIC TEST SEQUENCE Roll 2D6 Channel the Warp (Optional) Then, if one or more doubles or triples were rolled during this test, that model&#x27;s unit suffers D3 mortal wounds. If that model is not destroyed, the combined total of all the dice rolled during this test is the Psychic test result. If this equals or exceeds the Warp Charge value of the Ritual being attempted, that model manifests that Ritual and you resolve its effects. DESTINY&#x27;S RUIN (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 5 Select one enemy unit within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model. Until the end of the phase, each time a THOUSAND SONS or SCINTILLATING LEGIONS model from your army makes an attack that targets that unit, re-roll a Hit roll of 1. If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 10+, you can re-roll the Hit roll instead. TEMPORAL SURGE (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 6 Select one friendly THOUSAND SONS or SCINTILLATING LEGIONS unit that is not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units and is within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model. That unit can make a Normal move of up to D6&quot;. If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 10+, that unit can make a Normal move of up to 6&quot; instead. In either case, until the end of the turn, that unit is not eligible to declare a charge . DOOMBOLT (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 7 Select one enemy unit within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model (excluding units with the Lone Operative ability that are not part of an Attached unit and are not within 12&quot; of the manifesting model); that unit suffers D3 mortal wounds . If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 11+, that unit suffers D3+3 mortal wounds instead. TWIST OF FATE (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 9 Select one enemy unit within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model. Until the end of the phase, each time a THOUSAND SONS or SCINTILLATING LEGIONS model from your army makes an attack that targets that unit, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 1. If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 12+, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 2 instead.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Cabal rituals and warp charge checks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Datasheet Abilities
<table><thead><tr><th>Ability</th><th>Units</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Cabal of Sorcerers</td><td><details><summary>13 units</summary>Ahriman<br/>Chaos Lord On Disc Of Tzeentch<br/>Daemon Prince of Tzeentch<br/>Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings<br/>Exalted Sorcerer<br/>Exalted Sorcerer on Disc of Tzeentch<br/>Infernal Master<br/>Magnus The Red<br/>Rubric Marines<br/>Scarab Occult Terminators<br/>Sorcerer<br/>Sorcerer In Terminator Armour<br/>Tzaangor Shaman</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is THOUSAND SONS , at the start of your Shooting phase , one or more models from your army with this ability can attempt Rituals from those listed below. To do so, select one model from your army with this ability that has not yet attempted a Ritual this turn and select one Ritual no model from your army has attempted to manifest this turn, then take a Psychic test for that model by following the sequence below. PSYCHIC TEST SEQUENCE Roll 2D6 Channel the Warp (Optional) Then, if one or more doubles or triples were rolled during this test, that model&#x27;s unit suffers D3 mortal wounds. If that model is not destroyed, the combined total of all the dice rolled during this test is the Psychic test result. If this equals or exceeds the Warp Charge value of the Ritual being attempted, that model manifests that Ritual and you resolve its effects. DESTINY&#x27;S RUIN (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 5 Select one enemy unit within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model. Until the end of the phase, each time a THOUSAND SONS or SCINTILLATING LEGIONS model from your army makes an attack that targets that unit, re-roll a Hit roll of 1. If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 10+, you can re-roll the Hit roll instead. TEMPORAL SURGE (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 6 Select one friendly THOUSAND SONS or SCINTILLATING LEGIONS unit that is not within Engagement Range of one or more enemy units and is within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model. That unit can make a Normal move of up to D6&quot;. If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 10+, that unit can make a Normal move of up to 6&quot; instead. In either case, until the end of the turn, that unit is not eligible to declare a charge . DOOMBOLT (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 7 Select one enemy unit within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model (excluding units with the Lone Operative ability that are not part of an Attached unit and are not within 12&quot; of the manifesting model); that unit suffers D3 mortal wounds . If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 11+, that unit suffers D3+3 mortal wounds instead. TWIST OF FATE (PSYCHIC) WARP CHARGE 9 Select one enemy unit within 24&quot; of and visible to the manifesting model. Until the end of the phase, each time a THOUSAND SONS or SCINTILLATING LEGIONS model from your army makes an attack that targets that unit, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 1. If the Psychic test result for this Ritual was 12+, improve the Armour Penetration characteristic of that attack by 2 instead.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Cabal rituals and warp charge checks.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>40 units</summary>Cerberus<br/>Chaos Land Raider<br/>Chaos Predator Annihilator<br/>Chaos Predator Destructor<br/>Chaos Rhino<br/>Chaos Thunderhawk<br/>Chaos Vindicator<br/>Daemon Prince of Tzeentch<br/>Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings<br/>Defiler<br/>Deredeo Dreadnought<br/>Falchion<br/>Fellblade<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Forgefiend<br/>Helbrute<br/>Heldrake<br/>Hell Blade<br/>Hell Talon<br/>Kairos Fateweaver<br/>Kratos<br/>Land Raider Achilles<br/>Land Raider Proteus<br/>Leviathan Dreadnought<br/>Lord of Change<br/>Magnus The Red<br/>Mastodon<br/>Maulerfiend<br/>Mutalith Vortex Beast<br/>Relic Contemptor Dreadnought<br/>Sicaran Battle Tank<br/>Sicaran Punisher<br/>Sicaran Venator<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Spartan<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite<br/>Typhon<br/>Whirlwind Scorpius<br/>Xiphon Interceptor</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>11 units</summary>Blue Horrors<br/>Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings<br/>Flamers<br/>Kairos Fateweaver<br/>Lord of Change<br/>Magnus The Red<br/>Pink Horrors<br/>Scarab Occult Terminators<br/>Screamers<br/>Sorcerer In Terminator Armour<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Chaos Spawn, Defiler, Mutalith Vortex Beast</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Chaos Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Chaos Thunderhawk<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Heldrake<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Blue Horrors, Sekhetar Robots</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Ahriman<br/>Chaos Lord On Disc Of Tzeentch<br/>Exalted Sorcerer<br/>Exalted Sorcerer on Disc of Tzeentch<br/>Infernal Master<br/>Sorcerer<br/>Sorcerer In Terminator Armour<br/>Tzaangor Shaman</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Pact of Sorcery</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Blue Horrors<br/>Flamers<br/>Kairos Fateweaver<br/>Lord of Change<br/>Pink Horrors<br/>Screamers</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> When mustering your army, unless specifically stated otherwise, you cannot select SCINTILLATING LEGIONS as your Army Faction .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Army faction restriction enforced during validation.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Tzaangors</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td>Sekhetar Robots</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. If every model in a unit has this ability, then each time a ranged attack is made against it, subtract 1 from that attack&#x27;s Hit roll .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Apply -1 to hit vs ranged attacks.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

<details><summary><span style="background-color:#fff4cc; padding:2px 6px; display:block;">World Eaters (11 out of 19 abilities supported)</span></summary>
### Army Rules
<table><thead><tr><th>Army Rule</th><th>Description</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Blessings of Khorne</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> If your Army Faction is WORLD EATERS , at the start of the battle round , you can make a Blessings of Khorne roll. To do so, roll eight D6. You can then use those dice to activate up to two Blessings of Khorne (see below). Each Blessing of Khorne specifies the dice results it requires (where a number is specified, a double or triple of that value or higher is required). You can only activate each Blessing of Khorne once per battle round. Any unused dice from the Blessings of Khorne roll are then discarded. Once activated, each Blessing of Khorne applies to all units from your army with this ability until the end of the battle round. Example: Ash makes a Blessings of Khorne roll, getting the following: 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 6, 6. First they use the two 6s to activate Warp Blades (which requires a double 5+), leaving the following dice: 1,2, 2, 2, 3, 4. They then use the two 2s to activate Unbridled Bloodlust. Now that two Blessings of Khorne have been activated, no more can be activated and the remaining dice are discarded. UNBRIDLED BLOODLUST You can re-roll Charge rolls made for this unit. RAGE-FUELLED INVIGORATION Each time a model in this unit makes a Pile-in or Consolidation move , it can move up to 6&quot; instead of up to 3&quot;. TOTAL CARNAGE Each time a model in this unit is destroyed by a melee attack, if it has not fought this phase, roll one D6: on a 4+, do not remove it from play. The destroyed model can fight after the attacking unit has finished making its attacks, and is then removed from play. MARTIAL EXCELLENCE Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability. WARP BLADES Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [LETHAL HITS] ability. DECAPITATING STRIKES Each time a model in this unit makes a melee attack that targets an INFANTRY unit, that attack has the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Blessings dice engine + effects.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

### Detachments

Once activated, each Blessing of Khorne applies to all units from your army with this ability until the end of the battle round. Example: Ash makes a Blessings of Khorne roll, getting the following: 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 4, 6, 6. First they use the two 6s to activate Warp Blades (which requires a double 5+), leaving the following dice: 1,2, 2, 2, 3, 4. They then use the two 2s to activate Unbridled Bloodlust. Now that two Blessings of Khorne have been activated, no more can be activated and the remaining dice are discarded. UNBRIDLED BLOODLUST You can re-roll Charge rolls made for this unit. RAGE-FUELLED INVIGORATION Each time a model in this unit makes a Pile-in or Consolidation move , it can move up to 6&quot; instead of up to 3&quot;. TOTAL CARNAGE Each time a model in this unit is destroyed by a melee attack, if it has not fought this phase, roll one D6: on a 4+, do not remove it from play. The destroyed model can fight after the attacking unit has finished making its attacks, and is then removed from play. MARTIAL EXCELLENCE Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability. WARP BLADES Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [LETHAL HITS] ability. DECAPITATING STRIKES Each time a model in this unit makes a melee attack that targets an INFANTRY unit, that attack has the [DEVASTATING WOUNDS] ability.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Blessings dice engine + effects.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deadly Demise</td><td><details><summary>43 units</summary>Angron<br/>Blood Slaughterer<br/>Bloodthirster<br/>Cerberus<br/>Chaos Land Raider<br/>Chaos Predator Annihilator<br/>Chaos Predator Destructor<br/>Chaos Rhino<br/>Chaos Thunderhawk<br/>Daemon Prince of Khorne<br/>Daemon Prince of Khorne with Wings<br/>Defiler<br/>Deredeo Dreadnought<br/>Falchion<br/>Fellblade<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Forgefiend<br/>Greater Brass Scorpion<br/>Helbrute<br/>Heldrake<br/>Hell Blade<br/>Hell Talon<br/>Khorne Lord of Skulls<br/>Kratos<br/>Kytan Ravager<br/>Land Raider Achilles<br/>Land Raider Proteus<br/>Leviathan Dreadnought<br/>Mastodon<br/>Maulerfiend<br/>Relic Contemptor Dreadnought<br/>Sicaran Battle Tank<br/>Sicaran Punisher<br/>Sicaran Venator<br/>Skarbrand<br/>Slaughterbound<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Spartan<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite<br/>Typhon<br/>Whirlwind Scorpius<br/>Xiphon Interceptor</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEADLY DEMISE From detonating ammo stores to corrosive innards or frenzied death throes, some targets are deadly even in defeat. Some models have Deadly Demise x&#x27; listed in their abilities. When such a model is destroyed , roll one D6 before removing it from play (if such a model is a TRANSPORT , roll before any embarked models disembark ). On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; suffers x&#x27; mortal wounds.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> On destruction, roll 6+ to deal mortals within 6&quot;.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Deep Strike</td><td><details><summary>11 units</summary>Angron<br/>Bloodcrushers<br/>Bloodletters<br/>Bloodthirster<br/>Chaos Terminators<br/>Daemon Prince of Khorne with Wings<br/>Exalted Eightbound<br/>Flesh Hounds<br/>Lord Invocatus<br/>Skarbrand<br/>Terrax-pattern Termite</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> DEEP STRIKE Some units make their way to battle via tunnelling, teleportation, high-altitude descent or other extraordinary means that allow them to appear suddenly in the thick of the fighting. During the Declare Battle Formations step, if every model in a unit has this ability, you can set it up in Reserves instead of setting it up on the battlefield. If you do, in the Reinforcements step of one of your Movement phases you can set up this unit anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If a unit with the Deep Strike ability arrives from Strategic Reserves, the controlling player can choose for that unit to be set up either using the rules for Strategic Reserves or using the Deep Strike ability. - Unit can be set up in Reserves instead of on the battlefield. - Unit can be set up in your Reinforcements step, more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Reserves placement in Reinforcements step; enforces &gt;9&quot; distance.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Feel No Pain</td><td>Chaos Spawn</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FEEL NO PAIN Some warriors refuse to be laid low, even by what should be fatal wounds. Some models have Feel No Pain x+&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Firing Deck</td><td>Chaos Rhino</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIRING DECK Some transports have firing hatches, ports or platforms from which embarked passengers can shoot. Some TRANSPORT models have Firing Deck x&#x27; listed in their abilities. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Chaos Thunderhawk<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Heldrake<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Some AIRCRAFT models have Hover&#x27; listed in their abilities. When you are instructed to Declare Battle Formations , before doing anything else, you must first declare which models from your army with this ability will be in Hover mode. If a model is in Hover mode, then until the end of the battle, its Move characteristic is changed to 20&quot;, it loses the AIRCRAFT keyword and it loses all associated rules for being an AIRCRAFT model. Models in Hover mode do not start the battle in Reserves , but you can choose to place them into Strategic Reserves following the normal rules if you wish.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> No hover-specific handling.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Infiltrators</td><td>Goremongers</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> INFILTRATORS Many armies employ reconnaissance units who can sit concealed, waiting for the right moment to strike. During deployment, if every model in a unit has this ability, then when you set it up, it can be set up anywhere on the battlefield that is more than 9&quot; horizontally away from the enemy deployment zone and all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Forward deploy placement &gt;9&quot; from enemy zone/models.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Leader</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Khrn The Betrayer<br/>Lord Invocatus<br/>Lord on Juggernaut<br/>Master of Executions<br/>Slaughterbound</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Pact of Blood</td><td><details><summary>5 units</summary>Bloodcrushers<br/>Bloodletters<br/>Bloodthirster<br/>Flesh Hounds<br/>Skarbrand</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> When mustering your army, unless specifically stated otherwise, you cannot select BLOOD LEGIONS as your Army Faction .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Army faction restriction enforced during validation.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Scouts</td><td>Chaos Spawn, Eightbound, Lord Invocatus</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> SCOUTS Scouts form the vanguard of many armies. Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>

</details>

On a 6, each unit within 6&quot; of that model suffers a number of mortal wounds denoted by x&#x27; (if this is a random number, roll separately for each unit within 6&quot;). Example: A TRANSPORT model with the Deadly Demise D3 ability is destroyed. Before any models disembark and before removing it from play, its controlling player rolls one D6, getting a 6. There are three units within 6&quot; of that destroyed model, so its controlling player rolls one D3 for each of them, inflicting mortal wounds accordingly. - Deadly Demise x: When this model is destroyed, roll one D6. Each time a model with this ability suffers damage and so would lose a wound (including wounds lost due to mortal wounds ), roll one D6: if the result is greater than or equal to the number denoted by x&#x27;, that wound is ignored and is not lost. If a model has more than one Feel No Pain ability, you can only use one of those abilities each time that model suffers damage and so would lose a wound. - Feel No Pain x+: Each time this model would lose a wound, roll one D6: if the result equals or exceeds x&#x27;, that wound is not lost.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Post-damage roll to ignore wounds, including mortals.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Fights First</td><td>Chief Librarian Mephiston, Lion El&#x27;jonson, The Sanguinor</td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> FIGHTS FIRST Some warriors attack with blinding speed, landing their blows before their foes can react. Each time such a model is selected to shoot in the Shooting phase , you can select up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not already shot this phase. Then, for each of those embarked models, you can select one ranged weapon that embarked model is equipped with (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability). Until that TRANSPORT model has resolved all of its attacks, it counts as being equipped with all of the weapons you selected in this way, in addition to its other weapons. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot. - Firing Deck x&#x27;: Each time this TRANSPORT shoots, select one weapon (excluding weapons with the [ONE SHOT] ability) from up to x&#x27; models embarked within it whose units have not shot this phase; this TRANSPORT counts as being equipped with those weapons as well. Until the end of the phase, those selected models&#x27; units are not eligible to shoot.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Transports fire with selected embarked weapons; marks passengers as shot.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#fdecea"><td>Hover</td><td><details><summary>13 units</summary>Caestus Assault Ram<br/>Corvus Blackstar<br/>Fire Raptor Gunship<br/>Nephilim Jetfighter<br/>Ravenwing Dark Talon<br/>Sokar-pattern Stormbird<br/>Storm Eagle Gunship<br/>Stormfang Gunship<br/>Stormraven Gunship<br/>Stormtalon Gunship<br/>Stormwolf<br/>Thunderhawk Gunship<br/>Thunderhawk Transporter</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> HOVER Some aircraft can use vectored thrusters or anti-grav technology to hover over the battlefield, the better to hunt their prey or deploy embarked troops. Pack Leader With Jump Pack<br/>Wolf Lord on Thunderwolf<br/>Wolf Priest</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LEADER Mighty heroes fight at the forefront of battle. Some CHARACTER units have Leader&#x27; listed on their datasheets. Such CHARACTER units are known as Leaders, and the units they can lead - known as their Bodyguard units - are listed on their datasheet. During the Declare Battle Formations step, for each Leader in your army, if your army also includes one or more of that Leader&#x27;s Bodyguard units, you can select one of those Bodyguard units. That Leader will then attach to that Bodyguard unit for the duration of the battle and is said to be leading that unit. Each Bodyguard unit can only have one Leader attached to it. While a Bodyguard unit contains a Leader, it is known as an Attached unit and, with the exception of rules that are triggered when units are destroyed , it is treated as a single unit for all rules purposes. Each time an attack targets an Attached unit, until the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks, you must use the Toughness characteristic of the Bodyguard models in that unit, even if a Leader in that unit has a different Toughness characteristic. Each time an attack sucessfully wounds an Attached unit, that attack cannot be allocated to a CHARACTER model in that unit, even if that CHARACTER model has lost one or more wounds or has already had attacks allocated to it this phase. As soon as the last Bodyguard model in an Attached unit has been destroyed, any attacks made against that unit that have yet to be allocated can then be allocated to CHARACTER models in that unit. Each time the last model in a Bodyguard unit is destroyed, each CHARACTER unit that is part of that Attached unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time the last model in a CHARACTER unit that is attached to a Bodyguard unit is destroyed and there is not another CHARACTER unit attached, that Attached unit&#x27;s Bodyguard unit is no longer part of an Attached unit. It becomes a separate unit, with its original Starting Strength. If this happens as the result of an attack, they become separate units after the attacking unit has resolved all of its attacks. Each time a unit that is part of an Attached unit is destroyed, it does not have the keywords of any other units that make up that Attached unit (unless it has those keywords on its own datasheet) for the purposes of any rules that would be triggered when that unit is destroyed. Example: If you only destroy the Bodyguard unit that is part of an Attached unit, you have not destroyed a CHARACTER unit. If you only destroy the CHARACTER unit that is part of an Attached unit, or if you destroy the whole Attached unit, you have destroyed one CHARACTER unit. - Before the battle, CHARACTER units with the Leader ability can be attached to one of their Bodyguard units to form an Attached unit. - Attached units can only contain one Leader. - Attacks cannot be allocated to CHARACTER models in Attached units.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Attach Leaders during battle formations; protect Characters until Bodyguard is gone.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Lone Operative</td><td><details><summary>6 units</summary>Aethon Shaan<br/>Chief Librarian Mephiston<br/>Emperor&#x27;s Champion<br/>Kayvaan Shrike<br/>Lieutenant With Combi-weapon<br/>The Sanguinor</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> LONE OPERATIVE Assassins and other covert agents are difficult to track and pinpoint in the swirling maelstrom of battle. Aiming not for clinical kills but for maximum destruction over a wide area, they tear the heart from the enemy army. While this Mission Tactic is active, weapons equipped by ADEPTUS ASTARTES units from your army have the [SUSTAINED HITS 1] ability. MALLEUS TACTICS When the giants of war lumber forth, the Deathwatch will adopt Malleus tactics. Even the largest behemoth has a weak point, and the archives of the Deathwatch number them all. While this Mission Tactic is active, weapons equipped by ADEPTUS ASTARTES units from your army have the [LETHAL HITS] ability. PURGATUS TACTICS By adopting Purgatus tactics, the Deathwatch focus their deadly ire upon the commanders of the enemy host, assassinating them one after another with pitiless head shots and killing thrusts of the blade. While this Mission Tactic is active, each time an ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit from your army makes an attack, if a Critical Hit is scored, that attack has the [PRECISION] Unnoticed by the enemy, they range ahead of the main force. Some units have Scouts x&quot;&#x27; listed in their abilities. If every model in a unit has this ability, then at the start of the first battle round, before the first turn begins, it can make a Normal move of up to x&quot;, with the exception that, while making that move, the distance moved by each model in that unit can be greater than that model&#x27;s Move characteristic, as long as it is not greater than x&quot;. DEDICATED TRANSPORT models can make use of any Scouts x&quot; ability listed in their abilities, or a Scouts x&quot; ability that a unit that starts the battle embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model has (provided only models with this ability are embarked within that DEDICATED TRANSPORT model), regardless of how that embarked unit gained this ability (e.g. listed in their abilities, conferred by an Enhancement or by an attached CHARACTER , etc.). A unit that moves using this ability must end that move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models. If both players have units that can do this, the player who is taking the first turn moves their units first. Example: A unit has the Scouts 6&quot; ability. At the start of the first battle round, the controlling player can make a Normal move with that unit of up to 6&quot;. - Scouts x&quot;: Unit can make a Normal move of up to x&quot; before the first turn begins. - If embarked in a DEDICATED TRANSPORT , that DEDICATED TRANSPORT can make this move instead. - Must end this move more than 9&quot; horizontally away from all enemy models.<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Pre-game Scout move, including transport use when applicable.</details></td></tr><tr bgcolor="#e6f4ea"><td>Stealth</td><td><details><summary>8 units</summary>Aethon Shaan<br/>Captain In Phobos Armour<br/>Corvus Blackstar<br/>Eliminator Squad<br/>Kayvaan Shrike<br/>Lieutenant With Combi-weapon<br/>Scout Sniper Squad<br/>Sergeant Telion</details></td><td><details><summary>Description</summary><strong>Rules:</strong> STEALTH Some warriors are masters of disguise and concealment. Abhor the Witch, Destroy the Witch Each time this unit declares a charge , if one or more targets of that charge have the PSYKER keyword, you can re-roll the Charge roll . Melee weapons equipped by models in this unit have the [PRECISION] ability while targeting PSYKER units. Accept Any Challenge, No Matter the Odds Each time a model in this unit makes a melee attack, if the Strength characteristic of that attack is less than or equal to the Toughness characteristic of the target, add 1 to the Wound roll . Suffer Not the Unclean to Live This unit is eligible to declare a charge in a turn in which it Fell Back , and each time a model in this unit makes a Pile-in or Consolidation move , it does not need to end that move closer to the closest enemy model, provided it ends that move as close as possible to the closest enemy unit. Uphold the Honour of the Emperor If this unit has the INFANTRY keyword: - At the end of your Command phase , if this unit is within range of an objective marker you control, that objective marker remains under your control until your opponent&#x27;s Level of Control over that objective marker is greater than yours at the end of a phase. - If the mission you are playing features Actions , this unit is eligible to start to perform an Action in a turn in which it Advanced .<br/><strong>Engine:</strong> Vow selection with combat/objective effects.</details></td></tr></tbody></table>
